sentences.zh: 李適李適，字子至，京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: Li Shi, styled Zizhi, was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi, courtesy name Zizhi, was from Wannian in the Jingzhao region.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，再調猗氏尉。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was twice appointed magistrate of Yishi.
translations.idiomatic: After receiving his jinshi degree, he was twice posted as magistrate of Yishi.

sentences.zh: 武后修《三教珠英》書，以李嶠、張昌宗為使，取文學士綴集，於是適與王無競、尹元凱、富嘉謨、宋之問、沈佺期、閻朝隱、劉允濟在選。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu compiled the book Collected Pearls of the Three Teachings, appointing Li Jiao and Zhang Changzong as commissioners to gather literary scholars to compile it, Shi was then selected along with Wang Wujing, Yin Yuankai, Fu Jiamou, Song Zhiwen, Shen Quanqi, Yan Zhaoyin, and Liu Yunji.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu undertook the compilation of Collected Pearls of the Three Teachings, appointing Li Jiao and Zhang Changzong as commissioners to assemble scholars for the task, Shi was among those chosen, together with Wang Wujing, Yin Yuankai, Fu Jiamou, Song Zhiwen, Shen Quanqi, Yan Zhaoyin, and Liu Yunji.

sentences.zh: 書成，遷戶部員外郎，俄兼脩書學士。

translations.literal: When the book was finished, he was promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue and soon also served as a scholar of the Book Compilation Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Upon completion of the work, he was promoted to vice director in the Ministry of Revenue and soon added the concurrent post of compilation scholar.

sentences.zh: 景龍初，又擢脩文館學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jinglong era, he was further promoted to scholar of the Xiuxian Literary Hall.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Jinglong era, he was further elevated to a scholarship in the Xiuxian Literary Hall.

sentences.zh: 睿宗時，待詔宣光閣，再選工部侍郎。

translations.literal: During the reign of Emperor Ruizong, he awaited imperial orders at the Xuanguang Pavilion and was again selected as Vice Minister of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ruizong, he held a position awaiting imperial summons at Xuanguang Pavilion and was subsequently appointed vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 卒，年四十九，贈貝州刺史。

translations.literal: He died at the age of forty-nine and was posthumously granted the title of prefect of Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died at forty-nine; the throne conferred on him posthumously the title of prefect of Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 嘗夢與人論大衍數，寤而曰：「吾壽盡此乎！

translations.literal: Once he dreamed of debating the Dayan number system with someone; upon waking he said: "Has my allotted span of life reached its end?
translations.idiomatic: He once dreamed he was debating the Dayan divination numbers with another person. When he woke, he said, "Is this where my years run out?

sentences.zh: 」敕其子曰：「霸陵原西視京師，吾樂之，可營墓，樹十松焉。

translations.literal: " He instructed his son: "West of the Ba Ling plain one can look upon the capital — I find it pleasant; a tomb may be prepared there and ten pine trees planted.
translations.idiomatic: " He told his son, "From the west side of the Ba Ling plain the capital can be seen — I take delight in that place. Have a tomb prepared there and plant ten pines.

sentences.zh: 」及未病時，衣冠往，寢石榻上，置所撰《九經要句》及素琴於前，士貴其達。

translations.literal: " Before he fell ill, dressed in cap and robes he went there, slept on a stone couch, placed before him his own Essential Passages of the Nine Classics and a plain zither; gentlemen esteemed him for his comprehension.
translations.idiomatic: " Before illness took him, he went there in formal dress, lay on a stone couch with his Essential Passages of the Nine Classics and a plain zither set before him — men of learning admired his clarity of mind.

sentences.zh: 子 季卿子季卿，亦能文，舉明經、博學宏辭，調鄠尉。

translations.literal: His son Jiqing. Jiqing was also skilled in literature; he passed the Mingjing and Boxue Hongci examinations and was appointed magistrate of Huo.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Jiqing. Jiqing was also accomplished in letters; he passed both the classics and the erudite-literary examinations and received an appointment as magistrate of Huo.

sentences.zh: 肅宗時，為中書舍人，以累貶通州別駕。

translations.literal: During the reign of Emperor Suzong, he served as Secretariat Drafter and was demoted to vice prefect of Tongzhou on account of cumulative offenses.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Suzong he served as a drafter in the Secretariat, but repeated offenses led to his demotion to vice prefect of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 代宗立，還為京兆少尹，復授舍人，進吏部侍郎、河南江淮宣慰使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Daizong acceded, he was restored as vice magistrate of the capital district, again granted the post of drafter, and advanced to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel and Commissioner to Pacify Henan and the Jiang-Huai region.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Daizong came to the throne, Jiqing returned to serve as deputy magistrate of the capital, was again made a drafter, and was promoted to vice minister of personnel and commissioner for pacifying Henan and the Jiang-Huai region.

sentences.zh: 振拔幽滯，號振職。

translations.literal: He raised up those in obscurity and stagnation and was known as one who invigorated his office.
translations.idiomatic: He lifted men out of obscurity and neglect, earning a reputation for revitalizing his office.

sentences.zh: 大曆中，終右散騎常侍，遺命以布車一乘葬，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: During the Dali era, he died while serving as Right Regular Attendant of the Sanqi, left instructions to be buried in a single cloth-covered cart, and was posthumously granted Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career in the Dali era as right regular attendant of the palace guard and left orders to be buried in a single plain carriage; posthumously he was made minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 季卿在朝，薦進才髦，與人交，有終始，恢博君子也。

translations.literal: Jiqing, while at court, recommended and advanced talented men; in his dealings with people he had constancy from beginning to end — a broad-minded gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: While at court, Jiqing recommended gifted men and maintained his friendships steadfastly to the end — a man of generous and upright character.

sentences.zh: 初，中宗景龍二年，始于脩文館置大學士四員、學士八員，直學士十二員，象四時、八節、十二月。

translations.literal: At first, in the second year of Jinglong under Emperor Zhongzong, the Xiuxian Literary Hall first established four Grand Scholars, eight Scholars, and twelve Direct Scholars, symbolizing the four seasons, eight seasonal divisions, and twelve months.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, in the second Jinglong year of Emperor Zhongzong's reign, the Xiuxian Literary Hall was organized with four grand scholars, eight scholars, and twelve direct scholars — mirroring the four seasons, eight nodes of the calendar, and twelve months.

sentences.zh: 於是李嶠、宗楚客、趙彥昭、韋嗣立為大學士，適、劉憲、崔湜、鄭愔、盧藏用、李乂、岑羲、劉子玄為學士，薛稷、馬懷素、宋之問、武平一、杜審言、沈佺期、閻朝隱為直學士，又召徐堅、韋元旦、徐彥伯、劉允濟等滿員。

translations.literal: Thereupon Li Jiao, Zong Chuke, Zhao Yanzhao, and Wei Sili were made Grand Scholars; Shi, Liu Xian, Cui Shi, Zheng Yin, Lu Zangyong, Li Yi, Cen Xi, and Liu Zixuan were made Scholars; Xue Ji, Ma Huaisu, Song Zhiwen, Wu Pingyi, Du Shenyan, Shen Quanqi, and Yan Zhaoyin were made Direct Scholars; and Xu Jian, Wei Yuandan, Xu Yanbo, Liu Yunji, and others were summoned to fill the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiao, Zong Chuke, Zhao Yanzhao, and Wei Sili became grand scholars; Shi, Liu Xian, Cui Shi, Zheng Yin, Lu Zangyong, Li Yi, Cen Xi, and Liu Zixuan became scholars; Xue Ji, Ma Huaisu, Song Zhiwen, Wu Pingyi, Du Shenyan, Shen Quanqi, and Yan Zhaoyin became direct scholars; and Xu Jian, Wei Yuandan, Xu Yanbo, Liu Yunji, and others were called up to fill out the roster.

sentences.zh: 其後被選者不一。

translations.literal: Afterward those selected varied.
translations.idiomatic: The men chosen in later years varied.

sentences.zh: 凡天子饗會游豫，唯宰相及學士得從。

translations.literal: Whenever the Son of Heaven held feasts, gatherings, or pleasure excursions, only the chief ministers and scholars were permitted to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor hosted banquets or went on pleasure outings, only chief ministers and literary scholars were allowed to attend.

sentences.zh: 春幸梨園，並渭水祓除，則賜細柳圈辟癘；

translations.literal: In spring when he favored the Pear Orchard and performed water purification beside the Wei River, they were granted fine willow circlets to ward off pestilence;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, when the emperor visited the Pear Orchard and performed purification rites along the Wei River, they received delicate willow wreaths to ward off pestilence;

sentences.zh: 夏宴蒲萄園，賜硃櫻；

translations.literal: In summer when he feasted in the Grape Garden, crimson cherries were granted;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, at banquets in the Grape Garden, they were given scarlet cherries;

sentences.zh: 秋登慈恩浮圖，獻菊花酒稱壽；

translations.literal: In autumn when he climbed the Cien Pagoda, chrysanthemum wine was presented to wish him long life;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, when he climbed the Cien Pagoda, they offered chrysanthemum wine to wish him long life;

sentences.zh: 冬幸新豐，曆白鹿觀，上驪山，賜浴湯池，給香粉蘭澤，從行給翔麟馬，品官黃衣各一。

translations.literal: In winter when he favored Xinfeng, passed through Bailu Abbey, ascended Mount Li, they were granted bathing in the hot spring pool, fragrant powder and orchid unguent were supplied, those accompanying the procession were given Xianglin horses, and each official grade received one yellow robe.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, when he toured Xinfeng, visited Bailu Abbey, and ascended Mount Li, they were granted baths in the hot springs, supplied with scented powders and orchid oils, given Xianglin steeds for the journey, and each rank of attendant received a yellow robe.

sentences.zh: 帝有所感即賦詩，學士皆屬和。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor was moved by something he would compose a poem, and the scholars all contributed matching verses.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever something stirred the emperor to verse, the scholars would compose companion poems in reply.

sentences.zh: 當時人所歆慕，然皆狎猥佻佞，忘君臣禮法，惟以文華取幸。

translations.literal: People of the time envied and admired this, yet they were all familiar, crude, frivolous, and flattering, forgetting the rites and laws governing ruler and minister, relying solely on literary brilliance to win favor.
translations.idiomatic: Men of the day envied their position, yet these scholars were familiar to the point of vulgarity, frivolous and obsequious, heedless of the decorum owed between ruler and subject — they won favor through literary display alone.

sentences.zh: 若韋元旦、劉允濟、沈佺期、宋之問、閻朝隱等無它稱，附篇左雲。

translations.literal: Such men as Wei Yuandan, Liu Yunji, Shen Quanqi, Song Zhiwen, Yan Zhaoyin, and others had no other distinction worth mentioning; their biographies are appended herein.
translations.idiomatic: Figures such as Wei Yuandan, Liu Yunji, Shen Quanqi, Song Zhiwen, and Yan Zhaoyin had little else to their credit; their accounts are given below.

sentences.zh: 韋元旦韋元旦，京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: Wei Yuandan. Wei Yuandan was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yuandan was from Wannian in the Jingzhao region.

sentences.zh: 祖澄，越王府記室，撰《女誡》傳于時。

translations.literal: His grandfather Cheng was secretary of the Prince of Yue's household and authored Admonitions for Women, which circulated in his day.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Cheng had served as secretary to the Prince of Yue and wrote Admonitions for Women, which was widely read in its time.

sentences.zh: 元旦擢進士第，補東阿尉，遷左台監察御史。

translations.literal: Yuandan passed the jinshi examination, was appointed magistrate of Dong'e, and was transferred to investigating censor of the Left Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Yuandan earned his jinshi degree, took up the post of magistrate of Dong'e, and was promoted to investigating censor on the left.

sentences.zh: 與張易之有姻屬，易之敗，貶感義尉。

translations.literal: He had marital ties with Zhang Yizhi; when Yizhi fell, Yuandan was demoted to magistrate of Ganyi.
translations.idiomatic: As a relation by marriage of Zhang Yizhi, he was demoted to magistrate of Ganyi when Yizhi's faction collapsed.

sentences.zh: 俄召為主客員外郎，遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled as Vice Director of the Office of Chief Guests and was promoted to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled as vice director of the office of chief guests and promoted to drafter in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 舅陸頌妻，韋後弟也，故元旦憑以復進雲。

translations.literal: His uncle Lu Song's wife was the younger sister of Empress Wei; thus Yuandan relied on this to regain advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Because his uncle Lu Song was married to Empress Wei's younger sister, Yuandan was able to leverage the connection and climb back into favor.

sentences.zh: 劉允濟劉允濟，字允濟，河南鞏人，其先出沛國，齊彭城郡丞瓛六世孫。

translations.literal: Liu Yunji. Liu Yunji, styled Yunji, was a native of Gong in Henan; his ancestors came from Pei Commandery — a sixth-generation descendant of Huan, assistant magistrate of Pengcheng commandery in Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yunji, courtesy name Yunji, was a native of Gong in Henan. His family traced its descent from Pei — he was sixth in line from Huan, assistant magistrate of Pengcheng under the Qi.

sentences.zh: 少孤，事母尤孝。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he was especially filial toward his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Losing his father early, he was exceptionally devoted to his mother.

sentences.zh: 工文辭，與王勃齊名。

translations.literal: Skilled in literary composition, he was as renowned as Wang Bo.
translations.idiomatic: A master of prose and verse, he ranked in fame alongside Wang Bo.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，補下邽尉，累遷著作佐郎。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, was appointed magistrate of Xia'gui, and was repeatedly promoted to assistant in the Directorate of Historiography.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination he served as magistrate of Xia'gui and rose through successive appointments to assistant director of historiography.

sentences.zh: 采魯哀公後十二世接戰國為《魯後春秋》獻之，遷左史，兼直弘文館。

translations.literal: Collecting the twelve generations after Duke Ai of Lu connecting to the Warring States period, he compiled The Spring and Autumn After Lu and presented it; he was transferred to Left Historiographer and concurrently served on duty at the Hongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled The Spring and Autumn After Lu, linking the twelve generations after Duke Ai of Lu to the Warring States period, and presented it to the throne; he was then made left historiographer with concurrent duty at the Hongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 武后明堂成，奏賦述功德，手詔褒咨，除著作郎。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu's Bright Hall was completed, he submitted a rhapsody describing its merit and achievement; she personally wrote an edict praising and commending him and appointed him Director of Historiography.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu's Bright Hall was finished, he submitted a rhapsody celebrating its achievements; the empress responded with a handwritten edict of praise and appointed him director of historiography.

sentences.zh: 為來俊臣飛構當死，以母老丐餘年，繫獄，會赦免，貶大庾尉。

translations.literal: Framed by Lai Junchen on false charges, he was condemned to death; because his mother was old he begged for a few more years of life, was imprisoned, was pardoned when an amnesty was declared, and was demoted to magistrate of Dayu.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Junchen fabricated charges against him and he faced execution; citing his elderly mother, he pleaded for a reprieve and was imprisoned until an amnesty spared him — after which he was demoted to magistrate of Dayu.

sentences.zh: 復為著作佐郎，修國史。

translations.literal: He was again made assistant director of historiography and compiled the national history.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to his post as assistant historiographer and resumed work on the national annals.

sentences.zh: 常曰：「史官善惡必書，使驕主賊臣懼，此權顧輕哉？

translations.literal: He often said: "Historiographers must record good and evil without fail, so that arrogant rulers and treacherous ministers may fear — can this authority be considered light?
translations.idiomatic: He often remarked, "A historian must inscribe every good deed and every crime, so that arrogant sovereigns and villainous ministers will tremble — how could such power be deemed insignificant?

sentences.zh: 而班生受金，陳壽求米，僕乃視如浮雲耳。

translations.literal: Yet Ban Sheng accepted gold and Chen Shou sought rice — I regard such things as floating clouds."
translations.idiomatic: When Ban Gu took gold and Chen Shou demanded grain, I treated those things as no more than drifting clouds."

sentences.zh: 」遷鳳閣舍人，坐二張昵狎，除青州長史，有清白稱，巡察使路敬潛言狀。

translations.literal: " He was transferred to drafter of the Phoenix Pavilion; because of his intimacy with the Two Zhangs he was dismissed as chief administrator of Qingzhou, where he had a reputation for integrity; inspector Lu Jingqian reported on his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: " He was made a drafter at the Phoenix Pavilion, but closeness with the Zhang brothers cost him the post; appointed chief administrator of Qingzhou, he earned a reputation for integrity that the inspection commissioner Lu Jingqian commended in his report.

sentences.zh: 以內憂去官。

translations.literal: He left office due to a death in the family.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned to observe mourning for a close relative.

sentences.zh: 服除，召為修文館學士，既久斥，喜甚，與家人樂飲，數日卒。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was summoned as scholar of the Xiuxian Literary Hall; having long been banished, he was overjoyed, drank and made merry with his family, and died within several days.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning period ended, he was recalled as a scholar of the Xiuxian Literary Hall. After long exile he was elated, celebrated with his family — and died within days.

sentences.zh: 沈佺期沈佺期，字雲卿，相州內黃人。

translations.literal: Shen Quanqi. Shen Quanqi, styled Yunqing, was a native of Neihuang in Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Quanqi, courtesy name Yunqing, was from Neihuang in Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 及進士第，由協律郎累除給事中，考功受賕，劾未究，會張易之敗，遂長流驩州。

translations.literal: Having passed the jinshi examination, starting from Director of Music Harmonization he was repeatedly promoted to Supervising Censor; he accepted bribes in the Examination Bureau, and before the investigation concluded, when Zhang Yizhi fell he was exiled for life to Huanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After earning his jinshi degree he rose from director of music harmonization through successive posts to supervising censor; charged with taking bribes in the examination office, he was still under investigation when Zhang Yizhi's downfall brought him perpetual exile to Huanzhou.

sentences.zh: 稍遷台州錄事參軍事。

translations.literal: He was gradually transferred to recording secretary of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was eventually reassigned as recording secretary in Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 入計，得召見，拜起居郎兼修文館直學士。

translations.literal: When he came to the capital for the annual review, he was granted an audience, appointed Attendant of Imperial Movements, and concurrently made direct scholar of the Xiuxian Literary Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On arriving at court for his annual account, he gained an audience and was appointed attendant on imperial movements, with a concurrent post as direct scholar in the Xiuxian Literary Hall.

sentences.zh: 既侍宴，帝詔學士等舞《回波》，佺期為弄辭悅帝，還賜牙、緋。

translations.literal: After attending a banquet, the emperor ordered the scholars to perform the Huibo dance; Quanqi composed playful verses that pleased the emperor, who on his return granted him an ivory pin and crimson robe.
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet the emperor had the scholars perform the Huibo dance; Quanqi's witty verses delighted him, and on leaving the emperor bestowed on him an ivory tally and crimson robes.

sentences.zh: 尋曆中書舍人、太子少詹事。

translations.literal: Soon he successively served as Secretariat Drafter and Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to serve as drafter in the Secretariat and junior mentor to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 開元初卒。

translations.literal: He died at the beginning of the Kaiyuan era.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in the Kaiyuan era.

sentences.zh: 弟全交、全宇，皆有才章而不逮佺期。

translations.literal: His younger brothers Quanjiao and Quanyu both had literary talent but did not match Quanqi.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brothers Quanjiao and Quanyu were both skilled writers but never equaled Quanqi.

sentences.zh: 宋之問宋之問，字延清，一名少連，汾州人。

translations.literal: Song Zhiwen. Song Zhiwen, styled Yanqing, also named Shaoilian, was a native of Fenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Song Zhiwen, courtesy name Yanqing, also known as Shaoilian, was from Fenzhou.

sentences.zh: 父令文，高宗時為東臺詳正學士。

translations.literal: His father Lingwen, during the reign of Emperor Gaozong, served as Erudite of Detailed Verification of the Eastern Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lingwen had served under Emperor Gaozong as an erudite for textual verification in the eastern directorate.

sentences.zh: 之問偉儀貌，雄於辯。

translations.literal: Zhiwen had an imposing appearance and excelled in debate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiwen cut a striking figure and was formidable in argument.

sentences.zh: 甫冠，武后召與楊炯分直習藝館。

translations.literal: Just upon reaching adulthood, Empress Wu summoned him together with Yang Jiong to share duty at the Art Training Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Barely out of his teens, he was summoned by Empress Wu to share attendant duty at the Art Training Institute with Yang Jiong.

sentences.zh: 累轉尚方監丞、左奉宸內供奉。

translations.literal: Through repeated promotions he became assistant director of the Palace Manufactories and inner attendant of the Left Fengchen Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive appointments to assistant director of the palace manufactories and inner attendant of the Left Fengchen Guard.

sentences.zh: 武后游洛南龍門，詔從臣賦詩，左史東方蚪詩先成，后賜錦袍，之問俄頃獻，后覽之嗟賞，更奪袍以賜。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu visited the Longmen south of Luoyang, she ordered the attending ministers to compose poems; Left Historiographer Dongfang Jiu finished his poem first and the empress granted him a brocade robe; within moments Zhiwen submitted his poem, and after reading it she sighed in admiration and took back the robe to grant it to him instead.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu toured Longmen south of Luoyang and ordered her attendants to compose verses, Left Historiographer Dongfang Jiu finished first and received a brocade robe; moments later Zhiwen presented his poem — the empress read it with admiration, reclaimed the robe, and gave it to him instead.

sentences.zh: 于時張易之等烝昵寵甚，之問與閻朝隱、沈佺期、劉允濟傾心媚附，易之所賦諸篇，盡之問、朝隱所為，至為易之奉溺器。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Yizhi and others enjoyed extremely close favor through improper intimacy; Zhiwen together with Yan Zhaoyin, Shen Quanqi, and Liu Yunji devoted themselves to fawning flattery; every piece Zhang Yizhi recited had been written by Zhiwen and Zhaoyin — they even attended to Yizhi's chamber pot.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yizhi and his circle then held sway through scandalous intimacy; Zhiwen, Yan Zhaoyin, Shen Quanqi, and Liu Yunji lavished them with adulation — Yizhi's poems were all ghostwritten by Zhiwen and Zhaoyin, and the men stooped even to holding his chamber pot.

sentences.zh: 及敗，貶瀧州，朝隱崖州，並參軍事。

translations.literal: When they fell, Zhiwen was demoted to Longzhou and Zhaoyin to Yazhou — both as military retainers.
translations.idiomatic: When the faction collapsed, Zhiwen was exiled to Longzhou and Zhaoyin to Yazhou, each reduced to a staff officer.

sentences.zh: 之問逃歸洛陽，匿張仲之家。

translations.literal: Zhiwen fled back to Luoyang and hid in the home of Zhang Zhongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiwen slipped back to Luoyang and took refuge in Zhang Zhongzhi's household.

sentences.zh: 會武三思復用事，仲之與王同皎謀殺三思安王室，之問得其實，令兄子曇與冉祖雍上急變，因丐贖罪，由是擢鴻臚主簿，天下醜其行。

translations.literal: When Wu Sansi regained power, Zhongzhi together with Wang Tongjiao plotted to kill Sansi to secure the throne for the imperial house; Zhiwen learned the truth and had his nephew's son Tan together with Ran Zuyong report the emergency; thereby begging redemption from punishment, he was promoted to chief clerk of the Court of State Ceremonial — the whole realm despised his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: As Wu Sansi regained influence, Zhang Zhongzhi joined Wang Tongjiao in a plot to assassinate Sansi for the sake of the throne; Zhiwen learned of the plan and had his grand-nephew Tan and Ran Zuyong file an urgent denunciation, trading intelligence for clemency — he was made chief clerk of the Court of State Ceremonial, and the empire reviled him for it.

sentences.zh: 景龍中，遷考功員外郎，諂事太平公主，故見用。

translations.literal: During the Jinglong era, he was promoted to Vice Director of the Examination Bureau; he fawned upon Princess Taiping and therefore was employed.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jinglong era he was made vice director of the examination bureau through fawning service to Princess Taiping, which kept him in favor.

sentences.zh: 及安樂公主權盛，復往諧結，故太平深疾之。

translations.literal: When Princess Anle's power grew, he again went to ingratiate himself with her, so Taiping deeply resented him.
translations.idiomatic: When Princess Anle's influence rose, he courted her as well — earning Princess Taiping's deep resentment.

sentences.zh: 中宗將用為中書舍人，太平發其知貢舉時賕餉狼藉，下遷汴州長史，未行，改越州長史。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhongzong was about to appoint him Secretariat Drafter, but Taiping exposed his disorderly acceptance of bribes when supervising the examinations; he was demoted to chief administrator of Bianzhou, and before he departed the appointment was changed to chief administrator of Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhongzong was poised to make him a Secretariat drafter when Princess Taiping exposed the flagrant bribes he had taken as chief examiner; demoted to chief administrator of Bianzhou, he was reassigned to Yuezhou before he could depart.

sentences.zh: 頗自力為政。

translations.literal: He exerted himself considerably in administering affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He applied himself diligently to governing.

sentences.zh: 窮歷剡溪山，置酒賦詩，流布京師，人人傳諷。

translations.literal: He thoroughly traversed the mountains of Shan Creek, set out wine and composed poems that circulated to the capital, where everyone passed them around and recited them.
translations.idiomatic: He toured every corner of the Shan Creek region, composing poetry over wine; his verses reached the capital and were on everyone's lips.

sentences.zh: 睿宗立，以獪險盈惡詔流欽州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ruizong acceded, by edict he was exiled to Qinzhou for being cunning, treacherous, and overflowing with wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong came to the throne, an edict exiled him to Qinzhou for treachery, craft, and accumulated villainy.

sentences.zh: 祖雍歷中書舍人、刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: Zuyong successively served as Secretariat Drafter and Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Zuyong had served as drafter in the Secretariat and vice minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 倡飲省中，為御史劾奏，貶蘄州刺史。

translations.literal: He led revelry and drinking within the provincial offices, was impeached by censors, and was demoted to prefect of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He had hosted debauched drinking within the central offices, was impeached by the censorate, and was demoted to prefect of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 至是，亦流嶺南，並賜死桂州。

translations.literal: At this time he too was exiled to Lingnan and both were granted death by edict at Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Now he too was banished to Lingnan, and both men were ordered to take their lives at Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 之問得詔震汗，東西步，不引決。

translations.literal: Zhiwen, upon receiving the edict, shook and sweated, pacing back and forth, and did not take his own life.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict reached Zhiwen, he trembled and sweated, pacing this way and that without bringing himself to die.

sentences.zh: 祖雍請使者曰：「之問有妻子，幸聽訣。

translations.literal: Zuyong requested of the envoy: "Zhiwen has wife and children — I beg leave for a final farewell.
translations.idiomatic: Zuyong pleaded with the envoy, "Zhiwen has a wife and children — please allow us a final parting.

sentences.zh: 」使者許之，而之問荒悸不能處家事。

translations.literal: " The envoy consented, but Zhiwen was distraught and frenzied and could not put his household affairs in order.
translations.idiomatic: " The envoy agreed, but Zhiwen was too wild with terror to settle his household affairs.

sentences.zh: 祖雍怒曰：「與公俱負國家當死，奈何遲回邪？

translations.literal: Zuyong said angrily: "Together with you I have failed the state and deserve death — why this hesitation?
translations.idiomatic: Zuyong flared with anger: "You and I alike have betrayed the state and must die — why hesitate?

sentences.zh: 」乃飲食洗沐就死。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he ate and drank, bathed, and went to his death.
translations.idiomatic: " Then he ate, drank, washed himself, and went calmly to his death.

sentences.zh: 祖雍，江夏王道宗甥，及進士第，有名于時。

translations.literal: Zuyong, a nephew of Li Daozong, Prince of Jiangxia, passed the jinshi examination and was renowned in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Zuyong, a nephew of Li Daozong the Prince of Jiangxia, had passed the jinshi and was a name of note in his day.

sentences.zh: 魏建安後迄江左，詩律屢變，至沈約、庾信，以音韻相婉附，屬對精密。

translations.literal: From the Jian'an era of Wei down to the Jiangzuo period, the rules of poetry changed repeatedly; reaching Shen Yue and Yu Xin, they matched tones in harmonious combination and paired lines with precision.
translations.idiomatic: From the Jian'an period of Wei through the southern courts, poetic meter underwent many transformations; with Shen Yue and Yu Xin, poets began weaving tones into harmonious patterns and pairing lines with exacting precision.

sentences.zh: 及之問、沈佺期，又加靡麗，回忌聲病，約句准篇，如錦繡成文，學者宗之，號為「沈宋」。

translations.literal: When Zhiwen and Shen Quanqi came, they added further luxuriance, turning away from tonal faults, regulating lines to fit stanzas like brocade woven into patterns; scholars took them as models and called them "Shen-Song."
translations.idiomatic: Zhiwen and Shen Quanqi carried the art further toward ornate beauty, mastering tonal rules and shaping lines to fit each stanza like brocade in pattern — disciples took them as models and dubbed the school "Shen and Song."

sentences.zh: 語曰「蘇李居前，沈宋比肩」，謂蘇武、李陵也。

translations.literal: A saying runs: "Su and Li stand in the fore, Shen and Song shoulder to shoulder" — referring to Su Wu and Li Ling.
translations.idiomatic: As the saying has it, "Su and Li go before; Shen and Song stand abreast" — meaning Su Wu and Li Ling.

sentences.zh: 初，之問父令文，富文辭，且工書，有力絕人，世稱「三絕」。

translations.literal: At first, Zhiwen's father Lingwen was rich in literary composition and also skilled in calligraphy, with strength surpassing others — the age called these the "Three Unsurpassed."
translations.idiomatic: Zhiwen's father Lingwen was celebrated for three gifts: literary brilliance, mastery of calligraphy, and strength beyond any man's — the world called them the "three peerless talents."

sentences.zh: 都下有牛善觸，人莫敢嬰，令文直往拔取角，折其頸殺之。

translations.literal: In the capital there was an ox skilled at goring; no one dared approach it; Lingwen went straight up, pulled out its horn, broke its neck, and killed it.
translations.idiomatic: A bull in the capital was known for goring — no one dared go near it. Lingwen walked up, tore off its horn, broke its neck, and killed it on the spot.

sentences.zh: 既之問以文章起，其弟之悌以蹻勇聞，之愻精草隸，世謂皆得父一絕。

translations.literal: Since Zhiwen rose through literature, his younger brother Zhití became known for fleet courage, and Zhixùn excelled in cursive and clerical script — the world said each inherited one of the father's unsurpassed talents.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiwen made his name through writing; his brother Zhití won renown for swift valor, and Zhixùn mastered cursive and clerical script — each was said to have inherited one of their father's three gifts.

sentences.zh: 之悌，長八尺。

translations.literal: Zhití was eight chi tall.
translations.idiomatic: Zhití stood eight feet in height.

sentences.zh: 開元中，歷劍南節度使、太原尹。

translations.literal: During the Kaiyuan era, he successively served as military commissioner of Jiannan and governor of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaiyuan era he served successively as military commissioner of Jiannan and governor of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 嘗坐事流硃鳶，會蠻陷驩州，授總管擊之。

translations.literal: Once he was exiled to Zhuyuan on account of an offense; when barbarians captured Huanzhou, he was appointed commander-in-chief to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Banished to Zhuyuan for an offense, he was appointed supreme commander against the barbarians when they seized Huanzhou.

sentences.zh: 募壯士八人，被重甲，大呼薄賊曰：「獠動即死！

translations.literal: He recruited eight stalwart men, clad them in heavy armor, and charged close to the enemy shouting: "If the liao stir, they die!
translations.idiomatic: He enlisted eight stalwarts in heavy armor, charged the enemy line, and thundered: "Move, liao, and die!

sentences.zh: 」賊七百人皆伏不能興，遂平賊。

translations.literal: " Seven hundred of the enemy all fell prostrate unable to rise, and he thus pacified the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: " Seven hundred rebels collapsed where they stood and could not rise; the uprising was crushed.

sentences.zh: 之愻為連州參軍，刺史聞其善歌，使教婢，日執笏立簾外，唱吟自如。

translations.literal: Zhixùn served as military retainer of Lianzhou; the prefect, hearing he was skilled at song, had him teach a maid servant — each day holding a tablet he stood outside the curtain and sang freely.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixùn served as staff officer in Lianzhou; hearing of his gift for song, the prefect set him to training a maidservant — each day Zhixùn stood outside the curtain with his official tablet, singing with complete ease.

sentences.zh: 閻朝隱閻朝隱，字友倩，趙州欒城人，少與兄鏡幾、弟仙舟皆著名。

translations.literal: Yan Zhaoyin. Yan Zhaoyin, styled Youqian, was a native of Luancheng in Zhaozhou; from youth he and his elder brother Jingji and younger brother Xianzhou were all famous.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhaoyin, courtesy name Youqian, was from Luancheng in Zhaozhou. From early on he, his elder brother Jingji, and his younger brother Xianzhou were all well known.

sentences.zh: 連中進士、孝悌廉讓科，補陽武尉。

translations.literal: He successively passed the jinshi and the Filial Piety, Fraternal Duty, Integrity, and Forbearance examinations and was appointed magistrate of Yangwu.
translations.idiomatic: He passed both the jinshi examination and the filial-piety and integrity exam, and received appointment as magistrate of Yangwu.

sentences.zh: 中宗為太子，朝隱以舍人幸。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong was crown prince, Zhaoyin enjoyed favor as a drafter.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhongzong was still heir apparent, Zhaoyin won favor as one of his drafters.

sentences.zh: 性滑稽，屬辭奇詭，為武后所賞。

translations.literal: His nature was comical; his compositions were strange and uncanny, and he was appreciated by Empress Wu.
translations.idiomatic: He was by nature witty and grotesque in his phrasing — qualities Empress Wu admired.

sentences.zh: 累遷給事中、仗內供奉。

translations.literal: Through repeated promotions he became Supervising Censor and inner attendant of the imperial guard.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to supervising censor and inner attendant of the imperial guard.

sentences.zh: 后有疾，令往禱少室山，乃沐浴，伏身俎盤為犧，請代后疾。

translations.literal: When the empress fell ill, she sent him to pray at Mount Shaoshi; he bathed, prostrated himself on a sacrificial platter as an offering, and requested to take the empress's illness upon himself.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress fell ill, she dispatched him to pray at Mount Shaoshi; he purified himself, lay as a sacrificial victim on the offering tray, and begged to suffer her illness in her stead.

sentences.zh: 還奏，會后亦愈，大見褒賜。

translations.literal: Upon returning to report, it happened the empress had also recovered, and he received great commendation and reward.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned with his report, the empress had already recovered — and he was lavishly rewarded.

sentences.zh: 其資佞諂如此。

translations.literal: His talent for flattery was such as this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the depth of his sycophancy.

sentences.zh: 景龍初，自崖州遇赦還，累遷著作郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jinglong era, he returned from Yazhou upon receiving pardon and was repeatedly promoted to director of historiography.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Jinglong era he returned from exile in Yazhou under amnesty and rose through successive appointments to director of historiography.

sentences.zh: 先天中，為秘書少監，坐事貶通州別駕，卒。

translations.literal: During the Xiantian era, he served as Vice Director of the Secretariat; on account of an offense he was demoted to vice prefect of Tongzhou and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiantian era he served as deputy director of the secretariat, but an offense brought demotion to vice prefect of Tongzhou, where he died.

sentences.zh: 尹元凱尹元凱，瀛州樂壽人。

translations.literal: Yin Yuankai. Yin Yuankai was a native of Leshou in Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Yuankai was from Leshou in Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 由慈州司倉參軍坐事免，棲遲不出者三十年。

translations.literal: Starting as grain-store officer of Cizhou, he was dismissed on account of an offense and lingered in seclusion without emerging for thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: After serving as grain-store officer in Cizhou he was dismissed for an offense and lived in retirement without taking office for thirty years.

sentences.zh: 與張說、盧藏用厚，詔起為右補闕。

translations.literal: He was on close terms with Zhang Yue and Lu Zangyong; by edict he was summoned and appointed Right Remonstrance Official.
translations.idiomatic: Close friends with Zhang Yue and Lu Zangyong, he was recalled by imperial edict and appointed right remonstrance official.

sentences.zh: 時又有富嘉謨、吳少微，皆知名。

translations.literal: At that time there were also Fu Jiamou and Wu Shaowei, both well known.
translations.idiomatic: Also renowned at the time were Fu Jiamou and Wu Shaowei.

sentences.zh: 附 富嘉謨 吳少微嘉謨，武功人，舉進士。

translations.literal: Appended: Fu Jiamou and Wu Shaowei. Jiamou was a native of Wugong and passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Appended biographies: Fu Jiamou and Wu Shaowei. Jiamou was from Wugong and received his jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 長安中，累轉晉陽尉；

translations.literal: During the Chang'an era, through repeated transfers he became magistrate of Jinyang;
translations.idiomatic: In the Chang'an era he rose through successive posts to magistrate of Jinyang;

sentences.zh: 少微，新安人，亦尉晉陽，尤相友善；

translations.literal: Shaowei, a native of Xin'an, also served as magistrate of Jinyang and was especially friendly with him;
translations.idiomatic: Shaowei, from Xin'an, also served as magistrate of Jinyang and was his closest friend;

sentences.zh: 有魏穀倚者，為太原主簿，並負文辭，時稱「北京三傑」。

translations.literal: There was also Wei Guyi, who served as chief clerk of Taiyuan; all three were accomplished in literary composition and were called at the time the "Three Heroes of the Northern Capital."
translations.idiomatic: A third man, Wei Guyi, chief clerk of Taiyuan, joined them — all three were gifted writers and were known as the "Three Heroes of the Northern Capital."

sentences.zh: 天下文章尚徐、庾，浮俚不競，獨嘉謨、少微本經術，雅厚雄邁，人爭慕之，號「吳富體」。

translations.literal: Literary composition throughout the realm favored Xu and Yu — light and vulgar, without striving; Jiamou and Shaowei alone rooted themselves in classical learning, elegant, substantial, bold, and expansive; people competed to admire them, calling their style the "Wu-Fu school."
translations.idiomatic: The literary world favored the light, vulgar style of Xu Ling and Yu Xin; Jiamou and Shaowei alone drew on classical learning, writing in a refined, weighty, and vigorous manner that men everywhere sought to emulate — their style was dubbed the "Wu-Fu school."

sentences.zh: 豫修《三教珠英》。

translations.literal: He participated in compiling Collected Pearls of the Three Teachings.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in compiling Collected Pearls of the Three Teachings.

sentences.zh: 韋嗣立薦嘉謨、少微並為左台監察御史。

translations.literal: Wei Sili recommended Jiamou and Shaowei together as investigating censors of the Left Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Sili recommended both Jiamou and Shaowei for appointment as investigating censors on the left.

sentences.zh: 已而嘉謨死，少微方病，聞之為慟，亦卒。

translations.literal: Before long Jiamou died; Shaowei was then ill, and upon hearing of it was stricken with grief and also died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Jiamou died; Shaowei, already ill, was overcome with grief at the news and died as well.

sentences.zh: 劉憲劉憲，字元度，宋州寧陵人。

translations.literal: Liu Xian. Liu Xian, styled Yuandu, was a native of Ningling in Songzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xian, courtesy name Yuandu, was from Ningling in Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 父思立，在高宗時為名御史。

translations.literal: His father Silì, during the reign of Emperor Gaozong, was a renowned censor.
translations.idiomatic: His father Silì was a celebrated censor under Emperor Gaozong.

sentences.zh: 于時河南、北大旱，詔遣御史中丞崔謐等分道賑贍，思立建言：「蠶務未畢而遣使撫巡，所至不能無勞餞。

translations.literal: At that time Henan and the northern regions suffered great drought; an edict dispatched Vice Censor-in-Chief Cui Mi and others by separate routes to provide relief; Silì submitted a proposal: "Silkworm work is not yet finished yet envoys are sent on inspection tours — wherever they arrive there cannot fail to be labor and farewell feasts.
translations.idiomatic: When Henan and the north were stricken by severe drought, the throne dispatched Vice Censor-in-Chief Cui Mi and others on separate routes to distribute relief. Silì argued: "Silkworm season is not yet over, yet inspection envoys are already being sent — wherever they go, local people must labor to entertain them.

sentences.zh: 又賑給須立簿最，稽出入，往返停滯，妨廢且廣。

translations.literal: Moreover, relief distribution requires establishing ledgers and records, checking receipts and disbursements — going back and forth causes delays, and the hindrance and waste are extensive.
translations.idiomatic: Relief distribution also requires ledgers, audits of receipts and disbursements, and back-and-forth delays — the disruption and waste would be enormous.

sentences.zh: 若無驛處，馬須豫集，以一馬勞數家，今農事待雨興作，輟日役，破歲計，本欲安存，更煩擾之。

translations.literal: Where there are no relay stations, horses must be gathered in advance, and one horse burdens several households; now farm work awaits rain to begin — to suspend daily labor and ruin the year's plans, when the original intent was to preserve life, would only add further disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: Where there are no relay stations, horses must be requisitioned in advance, burdening several households per mount. Farm work now waits on rain to begin — suspending daily labor and wrecking the year's harvest plan defeats the very purpose of relief and adds fresh hardship.

sentences.zh: 望且責州縣給貸，須秋遣使便。

translations.literal: I hope the prefectures and counties may be charged to provide loans, and that envoys be dispatched conveniently in autumn.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that prefectures and counties be ordered to extend loans now, and that envoys be sent out conveniently in the autumn instead.

sentences.zh: 」詔聽，罷謐等行。

translations.literal: " The edict approved this, and Mi's mission was cancelled.
translations.idiomatic: " The throne accepted the proposal and cancelled Mi's mission.

sentences.zh: 遷考功員外郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Examination Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the examination bureau.

sentences.zh: 始議加明經帖、進士雜文。

translations.literal: He first proposed adding written examination papers for the Mingjing and jinshi degrees.
translations.idiomatic: He was the first to propose requiring written compositions for the classics and jinshi examinations.

sentences.zh: 卒官下。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died while still in office.

sentences.zh: 憲擢進士，調河南尉，累進左臺監察御史。

translations.literal: Xian passed the jinshi examination, was appointed magistrate of Henan, and was repeatedly promoted to investigating censor of the Left Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Xian earned his jinshi degree, served as magistrate of Henan, and rose through successive appointments to investigating censor on the left.

sentences.zh: 天授中，奉詔按來俊臣罪，憲疾其酷，欲痛繩之，反爲所構，貶潾水令。

translations.literal: During the Tianshou era, by imperial order he investigated Lai Junchen's crimes; Xian detested his cruelty and wished to punish him severely, but was in turn framed by him and demoted to magistrate of Linshui.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianshou era he was ordered to investigate Lai Junchen's crimes. Xian loathed Lai's cruelty and sought to punish him harshly, but Lai framed him instead and he was demoted to magistrate of Linshui.

sentences.zh: 俊臣死，召為給事中，轉中書舍人。

translations.literal: When Junchen died, Xian was summoned as Supervising Censor and transferred to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: After Junchen's death he was recalled as supervising censor and then made a drafter in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 坐善張易之，出為渝州刺史。

translations.literal: Because of his friendship with Zhang Yizhi, he was sent out as prefect of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His closeness to Zhang Yizhi led to his appointment as prefect of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 除太僕少卿，脩國史，兼脩文館學士，遷太子詹事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Director of the Imperial Stud, compiled the national history, concurrently served as scholar of the Xiuxian Literary Hall, and was transferred to Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice director of the imperial stud, worked on the national history, held a concurrent scholarship in the Xiuxian Literary Hall, and was promoted to mentor of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 時玄宗在東宮，雅意墳史，憲啟曰：「殿下位副君，有絕人之才，非以尋擿章句，要通大意而已。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Xuanzong was in the Eastern Palace and had a fondness for the classics and history; Xian submitted a memorial saying: "Your Highness stands as deputy to the ruler and possesses talent surpassing others — the aim is not to pick apart phrases and clauses, but to grasp the main meaning.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Xuanzong was crown prince, with a keen interest in the classics and history, Xian advised him: "Your Highness stands as heir to the throne and possesses extraordinary talent — the goal is not to parse every phrase but to grasp the larger meaning.

sentences.zh: 侍讀褚無量經明行脩，耆年宿望，宜數召問以察其言。

translations.literal: Your reader Chu Wuliang is versed in the classics and upright in conduct, an elder of long-standing reputation — he should be summoned frequently for questioning to examine his words.
translations.idiomatic: Your reader Chu Wuliang is learned in the classics and upright in conduct, a venerable elder of established reputation — summon him often and test his counsel.

sentences.zh: 」太子順納。

translations.literal: " The crown prince readily accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: " The crown prince accepted the advice.

sentences.zh: 會卒，贈兗州都督。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died and was posthumously granted the title of military commissioner of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after and was posthumously made military commissioner of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 武后時，敕吏部糊名考判，求高才，惟憲與王適、司馬鍠、梁載言入第二等。

translations.literal: During Empress Wu's reign, the Ministry of Personnel was ordered to conduct sealed-name examinations and evaluations to seek men of high talent; only Xian together with Wang Shi, Sima Huang, and Liang Zaiyan entered the second rank.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu, the Ministry of Personnel was ordered to conduct blind-marked examinations to identify exceptional talent; only Xian, Wang Shi, Sima Huang, and Liang Zaiyan placed in the second rank.

sentences.zh: 適，幽州人，終雍州司功參軍。

translations.literal: Shi was a native of Youzhou and ended his career as administrative aide of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was from Youzhou and ended his career as administrative aide in Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 鍠，河南人，神龍初，以中書侍郎卒。

translations.literal: Huang was a native of Henan; at the beginning of the Shenlong era he died while serving as Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Huang was from Henan and died early in the Shenlong era while serving as vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 事繼母孝，奉祿不入私舍。

translations.literal: He was filial toward his stepmother and did not bring his salary into his private quarters.
translations.idiomatic: He was devoted to his stepmother and never kept his official salary for himself.

sentences.zh: 與弟銓、伯父希象皆歷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Together with his younger brother Quan and his uncle Xixiang, all served as palace censors.
translations.idiomatic: He, his younger brother Quan, and his uncle Xixiang all served as palace censors.

sentences.zh: 希象，剛直不諂，終主爵員外郎。

translations.literal: Xixiang was upright and unflattering and ended his career as Vice Director of the Office of Hereditary Titles.
translations.idiomatic: Xixiang was upright and never obsequious, ending his career as vice director of the office of hereditary titles.

sentences.zh: 載言，聊城人，歷鳳閣舍人，專知制誥，終懷州刺史。

translations.literal: Zaiyan was a native of Liaocheng; he served as drafter of the Phoenix Pavilion, was specially charged with drafting edicts, and ended his career as prefect of Huaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zaiyan was from Liaocheng; he served as a drafter at the Phoenix Pavilion with special charge over edicts, and ended as prefect of Huaizhou.

sentences.zh: 李邕李邕，字泰和，揚州江都人。

translations.literal: Li Yong. Li Yong, styled Taihe, was a native of Jiangdu in Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yong, courtesy name Taihe, was from Jiangdu in Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 父善，有雅行，淹貫古今，不能屬辭，故人號「書簏」。

translations.literal: His father Shan had refined conduct, was thoroughly versed in ancient and modern learning, but could not compose prose — hence people called him "the book chest."
translations.idiomatic: His father Shan was a man of refined character, steeped in learning ancient and modern, but unable to write prose himself — men called him "the walking library."

sentences.zh: 顯慶中，累擢崇賢館直學士兼沛王侍讀。

translations.literal: During the Xianqing era, through repeated promotions he became direct scholar of the Chongxian Hall and concurrently reader to the Prince of Pei.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xianqing era he rose through successive appointments to direct scholar of the Chongxian Hall and reader to the Prince of Pei.

sentences.zh: 為《文選注》，敷析淵洽，表上之，賜賚頗渥。

translations.literal: He wrote a commentary on Literary Selections, expounding and analyzing with profound thoroughness, presented it to the throne, and received generous rewards.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote a commentary on Literary Selections with profound and thorough analysis, presented it to the throne, and received lavish rewards.

sentences.zh: 除潞王府記室參軍，為涇城令，坐與賀蘭敏之善，流姚州，遇赦還。

translations.literal: He was appointed secretary of the Prince of Lu's household, served as magistrate of Jingcheng, was exiled to Yaozhou on account of friendship with Helan Minzhi, and returned upon receiving pardon.
translations.idiomatic: He served as secretary to the Prince of Lu and as magistrate of Jingcheng, was exiled to Yaozhou for his friendship with Helan Minzhi, and returned under amnesty.

sentences.zh: 居汴、鄭間講授，諸生四遠至，傳其業，號「《文選》學」。

translations.literal: He lived between Bian and Zheng teaching; students came from the four directions, transmitted his learning, and it was called "the Literary Selections school."
translations.idiomatic: He taught between Bian and Zheng, drawing students from far and wide who carried on his work — the tradition was known as "Literary Selections studies."

sentences.zh: 邕少知名。

translations.literal: Yong was known from youth.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was already known in his youth.

sentences.zh: 始善注《文選》，釋事而忘意。

translations.literal: At first Shan annotated Literary Selections, explaining facts but forgetting meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Shan first annotated Literary Selections, explaining facts but missing the deeper meaning.

sentences.zh: 書成以問邕，邕不敢對，善詰之，邕意欲有所更，善曰：「試為我補益之。

translations.literal: When the book was finished he asked Yong about it; Yong did not dare reply; Shan pressed him, and Yong intended to make changes; Shan said: "Try to supplement and improve it for me.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was finished he asked Yong's opinion; Yong hesitated to answer. When Shan pressed him and Yong indicated he would revise it, Shan said, "Then try to improve it for me.

sentences.zh: 」邕附事見義，善以其不可奪，故兩書並行。

translations.literal: " Yong appended facts to reveal meaning; Shan, seeing that his work could not be displaced, therefore let both books circulate together.
translations.idiomatic: " Yong added explanations that brought out the meaning; Shan, finding his own work could not be set aside, allowed both commentaries to circulate together.

sentences.zh: 既冠，見特進李嶠，自言「讀書未遍，願一見秘書」。

translations.literal: After reaching adulthood, he visited Senior Grand Master Li Jiao and said of himself: "My reading is not yet complete — I wish to see the secret archives once."
translations.idiomatic: After coming of age he visited Senior Grand Master Li Jiao and said, "I have not yet read widely enough — I wish to spend time in the secret archives."

sentences.zh: 嶠曰：「秘閣萬卷，豈時日能習邪？

translations.literal: Jiao said: "The secret archives hold ten thousand scrolls — how could they be mastered in a short time?
translations.idiomatic: Jiao replied, "The secret archives hold ten thousand scrolls — how could anyone master them in a short while?

sentences.zh: 」邕固請，乃假直秘書。

translations.literal: " Yong pressed his request firmly, and Jiao therefore lent him temporary duty in the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: " Yong persisted, and Jiao granted him temporary access to the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 未幾辭去，嶠驚，試問奧篇隱帙，了辯如響。

translations.literal: Before long he took leave; Jiao was astonished and tested him with abstruse texts and hidden volumes — he answered with perfect clarity, as if echoing back.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he departed. Jiao, astonished, tested him with obscure texts and hidden volumes — Yong answered with perfect clarity, as if the answers echoed back instantly.

sentences.zh: 嶠歎曰：「子且名家！

translations.literal: Jiao sighed and said: "You are destined to be a master!
translations.idiomatic: Jiao sighed and said, "You are destined for greatness!

sentences.zh: 嶠為內史，與監察御史張廷珪薦邕文高氣方直，才任諫諍，乃召拜左拾遺。

translations.literal: When Jiao served as Director of the Secretariat, he together with investigating censor Zhang Tinggui recommended Yong for his lofty literary talent, upright spirit, and fitness for remonstrance; he was summoned and appointed Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiao became director of the Secretariat, he and investigating censor Zhang Tinggui recommended Yong for his literary brilliance, upright character, and fitness for remonstrance — Yong was summoned and appointed left reminder.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞宋璟劾張昌宗等反狀，武后不應，邕立階下大言曰：「璟所陳社稷大計，陛下當聽。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief Song Jing impeached Zhang Changzong and others for treason; Empress Wu did not respond; Yong stood below the steps and spoke loudly: "What Jing has presented concerns the great plan of the state — Your Majesty should heed it.
translations.idiomatic: When Vice Censor-in-Chief Song Jing impeached Zhang Changzong and others for treason and Empress Wu did not respond, Yong stood below the steps and declared loudly, "What Jing presents concerns the fate of the realm — Your Majesty must hear him.

sentences.zh: 」后色解，即可璟奏。

translations.literal: " The empress's expression relaxed, and she immediately approved Jing's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: " The empress's expression softened, and she immediately approved Jing's memorial.

sentences.zh: 邕出，或讓曰：「子位卑，一忤旨，禍不測。

translations.literal: When Yong went out, someone reproached him saying: "Your rank is low — one offense against the imperial will, and disaster is unforeseeable.
translations.idiomatic: As Yong left, someone reproached him: "Your rank is low — one word against the throne's will and disaster may follow.

sentences.zh: 」邕曰：「不如是，名亦不傳。

translations.literal: " Yong said: "If not for this, my name would not be transmitted either.
translations.idiomatic: " Yong replied, "Without acting thus, my name would never be remembered.

sentences.zh: 中宗立，鄭普思以方技幸，擢秘書監。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhongzong acceded, Zheng Pusi enjoyed favor through occult arts and was promoted to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhongzong came to the throne, Zheng Pusi won favor through occult arts and was promoted to director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 邕諫曰：「陛下躬政日淺，有九重之嚴，未聞道路橫議。

translations.literal: Yong remonstrated saying: "Your Majesty has personally governed for only a short time; within the ninefold palace there is solemnity — one does not hear reckless talk in the streets.
translations.idiomatic: Yong remonstrated: "Your Majesty has governed in person for only a short time; within the palace there is solemn dignity — one does not yet hear reckless talk in the streets.

sentences.zh: 今籍籍皆言普思馮詭惑，說妖祥，陛下不知，猥見驅使。

translations.literal: Now everywhere it is said that Pusi relies on deception and delusion, preaching omens and portents; Your Majesty is unaware and has unworthily been led to employ him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet everywhere men say Pusi traffics in deception and delusion, preaching omens and portents — Your Majesty, unaware, has been led to employ him.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：『《詩》三百，一言以蔽之，曰：思無邪。

translations.literal: Confucius said: "The three hundred poems — summed up in a single phrase: Have no depraved thoughts."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "Of the three hundred poems, one phrase covers them all: Have no depraved thoughts."

sentences.zh: 』陛下誠以普思術可致長生，則爽鳩氏且因之永有天下，非陛下乃今可得；

translations.literal: " If Your Majesty truly believes Pusi's arts can bring long life, then Shuangjiushi would have held the realm forever through them — it would not be Your Majesty who holds it today;
translations.idiomatic: " If Your Majesty truly believes Pusi's arts can grant immortality, then Shuangjiushi would have ruled forever through them — not Your Majesty today;

sentences.zh: 能致神人邪，秦、漢且因之永有天下，非陛下乃今可得；

translations.literal: If they can summon divine beings, then Qin and Han would have held the realm forever through them — it would not be Your Majesty who holds it today;
translations.idiomatic: If they can summon divine beings, Qin and Han would have ruled forever through them — not Your Majesty today;

sentences.zh: 能致佛法邪，梁武帝且因之永有天下，非陛下乃今可得；

translations.literal: If they can summon Buddhist dharma, then Emperor Wu of Liang would have held the realm forever through it — it would not be Your Majesty who holds it today;
translations.idiomatic: If they can summon Buddhist power, Emperor Wu of Liang would have ruled forever through it — not Your Majesty today;

sentences.zh: 能鬼道邪，墨翟、干寶且各獻其主，永有天下，非陛下乃今可得。

translations.literal: If they can practice the way of ghosts, then Mozi and Gan Bao would each have offered it to their lords and held the realm forever — it would not be Your Majesty who holds it today.
translations.idiomatic: If they can practice ghostcraft, Mozi and Gan Bao would each have offered it to their lords and ruled forever — not Your Majesty today.

sentences.zh: 自古堯、舜稱聖者，臣觀所以行，皆在人事，敦睦九族，平章百姓，不聞以鬼神道治天下，惟陛下省察。

translations.literal: From antiquity, Yao and Shun were called sage — I observe that their conduct lay entirely in human affairs: harmonizing the nine clans, bringing order to the common people; I have never heard of governing the realm by the way of ghosts and spirits — may Your Majesty reflect on this.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity, Yao and Shun were called sage because their conduct lay entirely in human affairs — harmonizing kin, ordering the people. I have never heard of ruling the realm through ghosts and spirits. I ask Your Majesty to reflect on this.

sentences.zh: 」不納。

translations.literal: " This was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor did not accept the remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 五王誅，坐善張柬之，出為南和令，貶富州司戶參軍事。

translations.literal: When the Five Princes were executed, because of his friendship with Zhang Jianzhi, Yong was sent out as magistrate of Nanhe and demoted to revenue officer of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the execution of the Five Princes, Yong's friendship with Zhang Jianzhi cost him his post — he was sent out as magistrate of Nanhe and demoted to revenue officer in Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 韋氏平，召拜左臺殿中侍御史，彈劾任職，人頗憚之。

translations.literal: When the Wei faction was suppressed, he was summoned and appointed palace censor of the Left Secretariat; in impeaching and performing his duties, people greatly feared him.
translations.idiomatic: After the Wei faction was suppressed, he was recalled as palace censor on the left; men feared his zeal in impeachment and office.

sentences.zh: 譙王重福謀反，邕與洛州司馬崔日知捕支黨，遷戶部員外郎。

translations.literal: When Prince Chongfu of Qiao plotted rebellion, Yong together with Luozhou vice prefect Cui Rizhi captured the accomplices; he was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Chongfu of Qiao plotted rebellion, Yong and Luozhou vice prefect Cui Rizhi captured the conspirators; he was promoted to vice director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 岑羲、崔湜惡日用，而邕與之交，玄宗在東宮，邕及崔隱甫、倪若水同被禮遇，羲等忌之，貶邕舍城丞。

translations.literal: Cen Xi and Cui Shi hated Cui Riyong, yet Yong was friendly with Riyong; Emperor Xuanzong was in the Eastern Palace, and Yong together with Cui Yinpu and Ni Ruoshui were all treated with honor — Xi and the others resented this and demoted Yong to assistant magistrate of Shecheng.
translations.idiomatic: Cen Xi and Cui Shi hated Cui Riyong, yet Yong maintained ties with him. While Xuanzong was crown prince, Yong, Cui Yinpu, and Ni Ruoshui all enjoyed favored treatment — Xi and his allies resented this and demoted Yong to assistant magistrate of Shecheng.

sentences.zh: 玄宗即位，召為戶部郎中。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong acceded, Yong was summoned as Director of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong came to the throne, Yong was recalled as director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 張廷珪為黃門侍郎，而姜皎方幸，共援邕為御史中丞。

translations.literal: Zhang Tinggui served as Vice Director of the Yellow Gate, and Jiang Jiao was then in favor; together they supported Yong for Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tinggui was vice director of the Yellow Gate, and Jiang Jiao was then in favor; together they secured Yong's appointment as vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 姚崇疾邕險躁，左遷括州司馬，起為陳州刺史。

translations.literal: Yao Chong detested Yong's treacherous and impetuous character and demoted him to vice prefect of Kuozhou; he was later raised to prefect of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chong disliked Yong's reckless and volatile character and demoted him to vice prefect of Kuozhou; he was later restored as prefect of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝封泰山還，邕見帝汴州，詔獻辭賦，帝悅。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned from performing the feng sacrifice on Mount Tai, Yong met the emperor at Bianzhou; by edict he presented a rhapsody and the emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: On returning from the feng sacrifice at Mount Tai, the emperor met Yong at Bianzhou; ordered to present a rhapsody, Yong pleased him.

sentences.zh: 然矜肆，自謂且宰相。

translations.literal: Yet he was arrogant and unrestrained, believing himself soon to become chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: But he grew arrogant and unrestrained, convinced he would soon become chief minister.

sentences.zh: 邕素輕張說，與相惡。

translations.literal: Yong had long looked down on Zhang Yue, and the two were mutually hostile.
translations.idiomatic: Yong had long despised Zhang Yue, and the two were bitter enemies.

sentences.zh: 會仇人告邕贓貸枉法，下獄當死。

translations.literal: It happened that an enemy reported Yong for taking bribes and perverting the law; he was imprisoned and faced execution.
translations.idiomatic: An enemy then accused Yong of bribery and abuse of law; he was imprisoned and condemned to death.

sentences.zh: 許昌男子孔璋上書天子曰：

translations.literal: Kong Zhang, a commoner of Xuchang, submitted a memorial to the Son of Heaven saying:
translations.idiomatic: Kong Zhang, a commoner of Xuchang, submitted a memorial to the emperor saying:

sentences.zh: :明主舉能而捨過，取才而棄行，烈士抗節，勇者不避死，故晉用林父不以過，漢任陳平不以行，禽息隕身不祈生，北郭碎首不愛死。

translations.literal: A wise ruler promotes ability and overlooks faults, selects talent and sets aside conduct; men of firm principle resist corruption, the brave do not shun death — therefore Jin employed Linfu despite his faults, Han appointed Chen Ping despite his conduct; Qin Xi gave his body without praying for life, Beiguo smashed his head without cherishing death.
translations.idiomatic: A wise ruler promotes ability and overlooks faults, selects talent and sets aside personal failings; men of principle stand firm, the brave do not flee death — thus Jin employed Linfu despite his faults, Han appointed Chen Ping despite his reputation; Qin Xi gave his life without begging to live, Beiguo smashed his skull without clinging to life.

sentences.zh: 向若林父誅，陳平死，百里不用，晏嬰見逐，是晉無赤狄之土，漢無天子之尊，秦不強，齊不霸矣。

translations.literal: If Linfu had been executed, Chen Ping had died, Baili had not been employed, and Yan Ying had been driven away — then Jin would have had no lands of the Red Di, Han would have had no imperial dignity, Qin would not have grown strong, and Qi would not have become hegemon.
translations.idiomatic: Had Linfu been executed, Chen Ping put to death, Baili passed over, and Yan Ying driven away — Jin would never have conquered the Red Di, Han would never have known imperial glory, Qin would never have grown strong, and Qi would never have become hegemon.

sentences.zh: 伏見陳州刺史邕，剛毅忠烈，難不苟免。

translations.literal: I humbly observe that Yong, prefect of Chenzhou, is resolute, loyal, and fierce, unwilling to accept unmerited escape from difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that Yong, prefect of Chenzhou, is resolute, loyal, and fierce — a man who will not accept unearned escape from danger.

sentences.zh: 往者折二張之角，挫韋氏之鋒，雖身受謫屈，而奸謀沮解，即邕有功于國。

translations.literal: In the past he broke the horns of the Two Zhangs and blunted the edge of the Wei faction; though he personally suffered demotion and humiliation, treacherous plots were thwarted and dissolved — thus Yong has rendered service to the state.
translations.idiomatic: In the past he broke the power of the Two Zhangs and blunted the Wei faction's thrust; though he suffered demotion and humiliation, treacherous plots were foiled — Yong has served the state.

sentences.zh: 且邕所能者，拯孤恤窮，救乏賙急，家無私聚。

translations.literal: Moreover, what Yong is capable of is rescuing the orphaned and pitying the destitute, relieving want and aiding the urgent — his household has no private hoard.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Yong rescues orphans, aids the destitute, relieves want, and helps the desperate — his household keeps no private hoard.

sentences.zh: 今聞坐贓下吏，死在旦夕。

translations.literal: Now I hear that on charges of corruption he has been handed to the officials and death is imminent.
translations.idiomatic: Now I hear he has been handed to the law on charges of corruption and faces death within days.

sentences.zh: 臣聞生無益于國者，不若殺身以明賢。

translations.literal: I have heard that one whose life brings no benefit to the state is better off giving his body to demonstrate worthiness in another.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that if one's life cannot serve the state, it is better to die demonstrating another man's worth.

sentences.zh: 臣願以六尺之軀膏鈇鉞，以代邕死。

translations.literal: I wish to offer my six-foot body to the axe and halberd in place of Yong's death.
translations.idiomatic: I offer my own body to the executioner's blade in Yong's stead.

sentences.zh: 臣與邕生平不款曲，臣知有邕，邕不知有臣，臣不逮邕明矣。

translations.literal: I and Yong were never close in life; I know of Yong, but Yong does not know of me — that I fall short of Yong is clear.
translations.idiomatic: Yong and I were never acquainted; I know of him, but he does not know of me — my inferiority to Yong is obvious.

sentences.zh: 夫知賢而舉，仁也；

translations.literal: To recognize worth and promote it is benevolence;
translations.idiomatic: To recognize worth and promote it is benevolence;

sentences.zh: 任人之患，義也。

translations.literal: To bear another's peril is righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: To bear another's peril is righteousness.

sentences.zh: 獲二善以死，臣又何求？

translations.literal: To gain both virtues through death — what more could your subject ask?
translations.idiomatic: To achieve both virtues through death — what more could I ask?

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下寬邕之死，使率德改行。

translations.literal: I humbly hope Your Majesty will spare Yong from death and let him lead by virtue and reform his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg Your Majesty to spare Yong and let him reform his conduct through virtue.

sentences.zh: 興林父、曲逆之功，臣得瞑目；

translations.literal: To revive the achievements of Linfu and Queni — your subject could close his eyes in peace;
translations.idiomatic: To revive the achievements of Linfu and Queni — I could die in peace;

sentences.zh: 附禽息、北郭之跡，大願畢矣。

translations.literal: To follow in the footsteps of Qin Xi and Beiguo — my greatest wish would be fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: To follow in the footsteps of Qin Xi and Beiguo — my dearest wish would be fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 若以陽和方始，重行大戮，則臣請伏劍，不敢煩有司，皇天后土，實聞臣言。

translations.literal: If, when spring warmth has just begun, a great execution is carried out again, then your subject requests to fall on his sword and dares not trouble the officials — Heaven above and Earth below truly hear my words.
translations.idiomatic: If, just as spring warmth begins, another great execution is carried out, I ask to fall on my sword myself rather than trouble the officials — Heaven and Earth hear my words.

sentences.zh: 昔吳、楚反，漢得劇孟則不憂，夫以一賢而敵七國之眾，伏惟敷含垢之道，棄瑕之義，遠思劇孟，近取於邕。

translations.literal: Formerly when Wu and Chu rebelled, Han had no worry once it obtained Ju Meng — for one worthy man can match the hosts of seven states; I humbly hope Your Majesty will extend the way of bearing stains, the principle of overlooking flaws, think far of Ju Meng, and take Yong from what is near.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu and Chu rebelled, the Han had no worry once Ju Meng was found — one worthy man can match the hosts of seven states. I humbly ask Your Majesty to practice forbearance, overlook flaws, recall Ju Meng from afar, and choose Yong from what is near.

sentences.zh: 況告成岱宗，天地更新，赦而復論，人誰無罪，惟明主圖之。

translations.literal: Moreover, the report of completion has been made at Mount Dai — Heaven and Earth are renewed; to pardon and then reconsider punishment — who is without guilt? Only a wise ruler should weigh this.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, with the rites completed at Mount Tai and Heaven and Earth renewed, to grant amnesty and then reopen the case — who is without fault? Only a wise ruler can judge this aright.

sentences.zh: 臣聞士為知己者死，臣不為死者所知，而甘之死者，非特惜邕賢，亦以成陛下矜能之慈。

translations.literal: I have heard that a gentleman dies for one who knows him; your subject is not known to the one for whom he would die, yet willingly accepts death — this is not merely to cherish Yong's worth, but also to fulfill Your Majesty's compassionate regard for ability.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that a gentleman dies for one who knows him. I am unknown to Yong, yet I gladly accept death — not only to preserve his talent, but to fulfill Your Majesty's merciful regard for ability.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，邕得減死，貶遵化尉，流璋嶺南。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Yong's death sentence was reduced; he was demoted to magistrate of Zunhua, and Zhang was exiled to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, Yong's death sentence was commuted; he was demoted to magistrate of Zunhua, and Zhang was exiled to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 邕妻溫，復為邕請戍邊自贖，曰：

translations.literal: Yong's wife Wen again petitioned on Yong's behalf to guard the frontier in self-redemption, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Yong's wife Wen petitioned again, asking that he be allowed to redeem himself by guarding the frontier, saying:

sentences.zh: :邕少習文章，疾惡如仇，不容於眾，邪佞切齒，諸儒側目。

translations.literal: Yong from youth studied literature, hated evil as he would an enemy, could not be tolerated by the multitude; the wicked and flatterers gnashed their teeth at him, and the Confucian scholars looked askance.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Yong devoted himself to letters and hated evil as an enemy; the crowd could not tolerate him, the wicked gnashed their teeth, and scholars looked on with suspicion.

sentences.zh: 頻謫遠郡，削跡朝端，不啻十載。

translations.literal: Repeatedly demoted to distant commanderies, he erased his traces from the court — no less than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Repeatedly banished to distant posts, he vanished from court for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 歲時歎戀，聞者傷懷。

translations.literal: Year after year he sighed with longing; those who heard were moved to sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Year after year he sighed with longing, and all who heard were moved to grief.

sentences.zh: 屬國家有事泰山，法駕旋路，邕獻牛酒，例蒙恩私。

translations.literal: When the state undertook rites at Mount Tai, as the imperial carriage returned by the route, Yong presented oxen and wine and by precedent received private favor.
translations.idiomatic: When the state performed rites at Mount Tai and the imperial procession returned, Yong presented oxen and wine and, by precedent, received the emperor's personal favor.

sentences.zh: 妾聞正人用則佞人憂，邕之禍端，故自此始。

translations.literal: Your handmaid has heard that when upright men are employed, flatterers grow anxious — the origin of Yong's disaster began from this.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that when upright men are employed, flatterers grow anxious — Yong's downfall began from that moment.

sentences.zh: 且邕比任外官，卒無一毀，天意暫顧，罪過旋生。

translations.literal: Moreover, in Yong's recent service in outer offices, in the end there was not a single blemish; Heaven's favor briefly looked upon him, and offenses immediately arose.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in his recent posts abroad Yong left not a single blemish on his record — Heaven's favor had briefly rested on him, and charges arose at once.

sentences.zh: 諺曰：「士無賢不肖，入朝見疾。

translations.literal: A proverb says: "Whether a gentleman is worthy or unworthy, once he enters court he meets with resentment.
translations.idiomatic: As the proverb says, "Whether a man is worthy or not, once he enters court he meets resentment.

sentences.zh: 」惟陛下明察。

translations.literal: " May Your Majesty discern clearly.
translations.idiomatic: " I ask Your Majesty to see this clearly.

sentences.zh: 邕初蒙訊責，便繫牢戶，水不入口者逾五日，氣息奄奄，惟吏是聽。

translations.literal: When Yong first faced interrogation and censure, he was immediately bound in the prison cell; for more than five days no water entered his mouth, his breath was faint, and he had no choice but to obey the clerks.
translations.idiomatic: When Yong first faced interrogation he was thrown into a cell; for more than five days he took no water, his breath grew faint, and he could only obey the jailers.

sentences.zh: 事生吏口，迫邕手書。

translations.literal: The matter arose from the clerks' mouths and forced Yong to write by hand.
translations.idiomatic: The case was fabricated by the clerks and Yong was forced to sign a confession.

sentences.zh: 貸人蠶種，以為枉法；

translations.literal: Lending someone silkworm seed was treated as perverting the law;
translations.idiomatic: Lending silkworm seed to a farmer was treated as abuse of office;

sentences.zh: 市羅貢奉，指為奸贓。

translations.literal: Purchasing silk as tribute offering was pointed to as corrupt bribery.
translations.idiomatic: Buying silk for tribute was called corrupt bribery.

sentences.zh: 于時匭使朝堂，守捉嚴固，號天訴地，誰肯為聞？

translations.literal: At that time the complaint-box envoys attended court, guards and arresters were strict and tight — crying to Heaven and appealing to Earth, who would report it?
translations.idiomatic: Complaint-box envoys attended court and guards were strict — who would hear a man crying to Heaven and Earth?

sentences.zh: 泣血去國，投身荒裔，永無還期。

translations.literal: Weeping blood he left the state and cast himself into the wild borderlands, with no hope of return.
translations.idiomatic: Weeping blood he left the realm for the wilderness, never to return.

sentences.zh: 妾願使邕得充一卒，效力王事，膏塗朔邊，骨糞沙壤，成邕夙心。

translations.literal: Your handmaid wishes that Yong may serve as a single soldier, exerting himself in the king's affairs, smearing his flesh on the northern frontier and fertilizing the sandy soil with his bones — fulfilling Yong's lifelong wish.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Yong be allowed to serve as a common soldier, giving his body to the northern frontier and his bones to the sand — fulfilling the wish of his heart.

sentences.zh: 表入不省。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted but received no response.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted but went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 邕後從中人楊思勖討嶺南賊有功，徙澧州司馬。

translations.literal: Later Yong followed the eunuch Yang Sixu in campaigning against bandits in Lingnan with merit and was transferred to vice prefect of Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yong followed the eunuch Yang Sixu against Lingnan bandits with distinction and was transferred to vice prefect of Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 開元二十三年，起為括州刺史，喜興利除害。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Kaiyuan, he was raised to prefect of Kuozhou and delighted in promoting benefit and removing harm.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 23 he was restored as prefect of Kuozhou and devoted himself to public benefit.

sentences.zh: 復坐誣枉，且得罪，天子識其名，詔勿劾。

translations.literal: Again he was charged with false accusation and faced offense; the Son of Heaven recognized his name and by edict ordered that he not be impeached.
translations.idiomatic: Again he faced false charges, but the emperor knew his name and ordered that he not be impeached.

sentences.zh: 後歷淄、滑二州刺史，上計京師。

translations.literal: Later he successively served as prefect of Zi and Hua and came to the capital for the annual review.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as prefect of Zi and Hua and came to the capital for his annual account.

sentences.zh: 始，邕蚤有名，重義愛士，久斥外，不與士大夫接。

translations.literal: At first Yong had early fame, valued righteousness and loved scholars; long banished outside, he had not associated with the gentry.
translations.idiomatic: Yong had been famous early, valued loyalty and loved scholars; long exiled, he had been cut off from the gentry.

sentences.zh: 既入朝，人間傳其眉目瑰異，至阡陌聚觀，後生望風內謁，門巷填隘。
