translations.literal: Once he entered court, word spread among the people of his striking and unusual appearance — crowds gathered to watch in the lanes; young men came in throngs to pay calls, filling the gates and alleys to overflowing.
translations.idiomatic: Once he entered court, word spread of his striking appearance — crowds gathered in the streets; young men flocked to his door until lanes and gates overflowed.

sentences.zh: 中人臨問，索所為文章，且進上。

translations.literal: Eunuchs came to inquire, requesting his written works and presenting them upward.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs came to inquire, requesting his writings and presenting them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 以讒媢不得留，出為汲郡、北海太守。

translations.literal: Because of slander and jealousy he could not remain and was sent out as prefect of Ji commandery and Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: Slander and jealousy kept him from staying at court; he was sent out as prefect of Ji and Beihai.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，左驍衛兵曹參軍柳勣有罪下獄，邕嘗遺勣馬，故吉溫使引邕嘗以休咎相語，陰賂遺。

translations.literal: During the Tianbao era, Liu Ji, military staff officer of the Left Xiaowei Guard, was guilty and imprisoned; Yong had once given Ji a horse, so Ji Wen had him implicate Yong as having spoken with him about fortune and misfortune and having given secret bribes.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianbao era Liu Ji, staff officer of the Left Xiaowei Guard, was imprisoned for an offense. Yong had once given him a horse, and Ji Wen had Liu implicate Yong for discussing omens with him and giving secret bribes.

sentences.zh: 宰相李林甫素忌邕，因傅以罪。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Li Linfu had long resented Yong and therefore attached guilt to him.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Li Linfu had long resented Yong and used the case to attach guilt to him.

sentences.zh: 詔刑部員外郎祁順之、監察御史羅希奭就郡杖殺之，時年七十。

translations.literal: By edict, Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice Qi Shunzhi and investigating censor Luo Xishi went to the commandery and beat him to death with the staff; he was then seventy years old.
translations.idiomatic: By edict Vice Director Qi Shunzhi and investigating censor Luo Xishi went to his commandery and beat him to death with the staff; he was seventy.

sentences.zh: 代宗時，贈秘書監。

translations.literal: During the reign of Emperor Daizong, he was posthumously granted Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Daizong he was posthumously made director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 邕之文，於碑頌是所長，人奉金帛請其文，前後所受鉅萬計。

translations.literal: Yong's writing excelled in stele inscriptions and eulogies; people offered gold and silk to request his compositions — the amounts he received before and after totaled tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Yong excelled at stele inscriptions and eulogies; men offered gold and silk for his compositions — his earnings totaled tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 邕雖詘不進，而文名天下，時稱李北海。

translations.literal: Though Yong was frustrated and did not advance, his literary fame filled the realm; men of the time called him Li of Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: Though Yong never reached high office, his literary fame filled the realm; his contemporaries called him Li of Beihai.

sentences.zh: 盧藏用嘗謂：「邕如干將、莫邪，難與爭鋒，但虞傷缺耳。

translations.literal: Lu Zangyong once said: "Yong is like Ganjiang and Moye — hard to contend against in sharpness, but one only fears he may chip and break.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zangyong once said, "Yong is like the swords Ganjiang and Moye — none can match his edge, but one fears he may chip and break.

sentences.zh: 」後卒如言。

translations.literal: " In the end it happened exactly as he said.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end it happened exactly as he said.

sentences.zh: 杜甫知邕負謗死，作《八哀詩》，讀者傷之。

translations.literal: Du Fu, knowing Yong had died bearing slander, composed the Eight Laments; readers were moved to sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Du Fu, learning that Yong had died under false accusation, wrote the Eight Laments — readers were moved to grief.

sentences.zh: 邕資豪放，不能治細行，所在賄謝，畋遊自肆，終以敗云。

translations.literal: Yong's nature was bold and unrestrained; he could not manage small conduct — wherever he went he accepted bribes and gifts, hunted and roamed at will, and in the end was ruined, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was bold and unrestrained, careless of small proprieties — he accepted gifts wherever he went, hunted and roamed at will, and in the end was ruined.

sentences.zh: 呂向呂向，字子回，亡其世貫，或曰涇州人。

translations.literal: Lu Xiang. Lu Xiang, styled Zihui, lost record of his ancestral home; some say he was a native of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xiang, courtesy name Zihui, lost record of his ancestral home; some say he was from Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 少孤，托外祖母隱陸渾山。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he was entrusted to his maternal grandmother and lived in seclusion on Mount Luhun.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned early, he was raised by his maternal grandmother in seclusion on Mount Luhun.

sentences.zh: 工草隸，能一筆環寫百字，若縈發然，世號「連錦書」。

translations.literal: Skilled in cursive and clerical script, he could write a hundred characters in one continuous circling stroke like coiled hair — the age called it "linked-brocade script."
translations.idiomatic: He mastered cursive and clerical script and could write a hundred characters in one unbroken circling stroke like coiled hair — the world called it "linked-brocade script."

sentences.zh: 強志於學，每賣藥，即市閱書，遂通古今。

translations.literal: Strong-willed in study, whenever he sold medicine he would buy books in the market to read, and thus became versed in ancient and modern learning.
translations.idiomatic: Fiercely devoted to learning, he sold medicine to buy books in the market and thus mastered learning ancient and modern.

sentences.zh: 玄宗開元十年，召入翰林，兼集賢院校理，侍太子及諸王為文章。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Kaiyuan under Emperor Xuanzong, he was summoned into the Hanlin Academy, concurrently served as collator of the Jixian Academy, and attended the crown prince and princes in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 10 Emperor Xuanzong summoned him to the Hanlin Academy as collator of the Jixian Academy, where he attended the crown prince and princes in literary matters.

sentences.zh: 時帝歲遣使采擇天下姝好，內之後宮，號「花鳥使」；

translations.literal: At that time the emperor each year dispatched envoys to select beautiful women throughout the realm for the inner palace — they were called the "Flower-and-Bird Envoys";
translations.idiomatic: Each year the emperor dispatched envoys to gather beautiful women for the inner palace — they were called the "Flower-and-Bird Envoys";

sentences.zh: 向因奏《美人賦》以諷，帝善之，擢左拾遺。

translations.literal: Xiang therefore submitted the Rhapsody on Beautiful Women as admonition; the emperor approved and promoted him to Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang submitted the Rhapsody on Beautiful Women as a subtle remonstrance; the emperor approved and promoted him to left reminder.

sentences.zh: 天子數校獵渭川，向又獻詩規諷，進左補闕。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven frequently hunted on the Wei River; Xiang again presented a poem of admonition and was advanced to Left Remonstrance Official.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor frequently hunted on the Wei River; Xiang again submitted a remonstrance in verse and was promoted to left remonstrance official.

sentences.zh: 帝自為文，勒石西嶽，詔向為鐫勒使。

translations.literal: The emperor himself composed a text and had it carved on stone at the Western Peak; by edict Xiang was made commissioner for carving and inscribing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor composed an inscription for the Western Peak and appointed Xiang commissioner for carving it in stone.

sentences.zh: 以起居舍人從帝東巡，帝引頡利發及蕃夷酋長入仗內，賜弓矢射禽。

translations.literal: As Attendant of Imperial Movements he accompanied the emperor on the eastern tour; the emperor led Ashina Facheng and tribal chieftains of the frontier peoples inside the guard formation, granting them bows and arrows to shoot birds.
translations.idiomatic: As attendant on imperial movements he accompanied the emperor's eastern tour; the emperor brought Ashina Facheng and frontier chieftains inside the guard formation and granted them bows to shoot game.

sentences.zh: 向上言：「鴟梟不鳴，未為瑞鳥；

translations.literal: Xiang submitted a memorial saying: "When the owl and the owl-like bird do not cry, they are not yet auspicious birds;
translations.idiomatic: Xiang submitted a memorial: "When owls do not cry, they are not yet auspicious birds;

sentences.zh: 豺虎雖伏，弗曰仁獸。

translations.literal: Though wolves and tigers lie low, they are not called benevolent beasts.
translations.idiomatic: Though wolves and tigers crouch low, they are not called benevolent beasts.

sentences.zh: 況突厥安忍殘賊，莫顧君父，陛下震以武義，來以文德，勢不得不廷，故稽顙稱臣，奔命遣使。

translations.literal: Moreover the Turks are cruel and treacherous, caring nothing for ruler and father; Your Majesty awed them with martial righteousness and drew them with civil virtue — they had no choice but to come to court, therefore kowtowing and declaring themselves subjects, rushing to dispatch envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the Turks are cruel and treacherous, heedless of ruler and father. Your Majesty awed them with martial force and drew them with civil virtue — they had no choice but to come to court, kowtow, and dispatch envoys in haste.

sentences.zh: 陛下引內從官，陪封禪盛禮，使飛矢於前，同獲獸之樂，是狎昵太過。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has led them inside among attendant officials, to accompany the grand rites of the feng and shan sacrifices, letting them shoot arrows before you and share the joy of taking game — this is excessive familiarity.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has brought them among attendant officials to share the grand feng and shan rites, letting them shoot before you and share the joy of the hunt — this is familiarity carried too far.

sentences.zh: 或荊卿詭動，何羅竊發，逼嚴蹕，冒清塵，縱醢單于，汙穹廬，何以塞責？

translations.literal: If Jing Ke should move by trickery, or Heluo should strike by stealth, pressing upon the imperial guard and defiling the clear dust — even if the Xiongnu chieftain were minced, and the felt tents defiled, how could responsibility be fulfilled?
translations.idiomatic: If a Jing Ke should move by treachery or a Heluo strike by stealth, pressing upon the imperial guard and defiling the imperial path — even if the chieftain were executed and the tents defiled, how could the blame be answered?

sentences.zh: 」帝順納，詔蕃夷出仗。

translations.literal: " The emperor readily accepted this and by edict ordered the frontier peoples out of the guard formation.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor accepted the advice and ordered the frontier peoples removed from the guard formation.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷主客郎中，專侍皇太子，眷賚良異。

translations.literal: After a long time he was transferred to Director of the Office of Chief Guests, specially attending the crown prince; favors and gifts were exceptionally generous.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was made director of the office of chief guests with special charge over the crown prince; imperial favor was exceptionally generous.

sentences.zh: 始，向之生，父岌客遠方不還。

translations.literal: At first, when Xiang was born, his father Ba had traveled to a distant place as a guest and did not return.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiang was born, his father Ba had traveled abroad as a guest and never returned.

sentences.zh: 少喪母，失墓所在，將葬，巫者求得之。

translations.literal: Young he lost his mother and did not know where the tomb was located; when about to bury her, a shaman was made to find it.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his mother young and did not know where she was buried; when the time came to inter her, a shaman located the grave.

sentences.zh: 不知父在亡，招魂合諸墓。

translations.literal: Not knowing whether his father was alive or dead, he summoned the soul and joined it to the other graves.
translations.idiomatic: Not knowing whether his father lived or had died, he performed a soul-summoning rite and joined the grave to the family plot.

sentences.zh: 後有傳父猶在者，訪索累年不獲。

translations.literal: Later there were reports that his father was still alive; he searched for many years without finding him.
translations.idiomatic: Later word came that his father might still be alive; he searched for years without success.

sentences.zh: 它日自朝還，道見一老人，物色問之，果父也。

translations.literal: One day returning from court, on the road he saw an old man; scrutinizing and questioning him, it turned out to be his father.
translations.idiomatic: One day returning from court he met an old man on the road; questioning him closely, he found it was his father.

sentences.zh: 下馬抱父足號慟，行人為流涕。

translations.literal: He dismounted, embraced his father's feet, and wailed in grief; passersby shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: He dismounted, clutched his father's feet, and wailed; passersby wept.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，咨歎，官岌朝散大夫，賜錦彩，給內教坊樂工，娛懌其心。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, he sighed with admiration, appointed Ba Grand Master of Palace Attendance, granted brocade and colored silks, and supplied musicians from the Inner Music Office to delight his heart.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard, he sighed with admiration, made Ba a grand master of palace attendance, granted brocades, and supplied musicians from the inner music office to delight him.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈東平太守。

translations.literal: When he died, he was posthumously granted Prefect of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made prefect of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 向終喪，再遷中書舍人，改工部侍郎。

translations.literal: After Xiang completed mourning, he was twice transferred to Secretariat Drafter and then changed to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: After completing mourning, Xiang was promoted to drafter in the Secretariat and then to vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈華陰太守。

translations.literal: When he died, he was posthumously granted Prefect of Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made prefect of Huayin.

sentences.zh: 嘗以李善釋《文選》為繁釀，與呂延濟、劉良、張銑、李周翰等更為詁解，時號《五臣注》。

translations.literal: He once considered Li Shan's commentary on Literary Selections overly elaborate; together with Lu Yanji, Liu Liang, Zhang Xian, Li Zhouhan, and others he produced a new glossed explanation, called at the time the Five Ministers Commentary.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Li Shan's commentary on Literary Selections overly elaborate, he joined Lu Yanji, Liu Liang, Zhang Xian, Li Zhouhan, and others in a new gloss — known as the Five Ministers Commentary.

sentences.zh: 王翰王翰，字子羽，并州晉陽人。

translations.literal: Wang Han. Wang Han, styled Ziyu, was a native of Jinyang in Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Han, courtesy name Ziyu, was from Jinyang in Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 少豪健恃才，及進士第，然喜蒱酒。

translations.literal: Young he was bold, robust, and relied on his talent; he passed the jinshi examination, yet delighted in gambling and wine.
translations.idiomatic: Bold and confident in youth, he earned his jinshi degree but loved gambling and wine.

sentences.zh: 張嘉貞為本州長史，偉其人，厚遇之。

translations.literal: Zhang Jiazhen served as chief administrator of the province and admired him as a great man, treating him generously.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiazhen, chief administrator of the province, admired him and treated him generously.

sentences.zh: 翰自歌以舞屬嘉貞，神氣軒舉自如。

translations.literal: Han himself sang and danced to toast Jiazhen, his spirit lofty and at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Han sang and danced to toast Jiazhen, his spirit lofty and utterly at ease.

sentences.zh: 張說至，禮益加。

translations.literal: When Zhang Yue arrived, courtesy toward him increased further.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yue arrived, the honors paid him grew even greater.

sentences.zh: 復舉直言極諫，調昌樂尉，又舉超拔君類。

translations.literal: He again passed the examination for forthright speech and extreme remonstrance, was appointed magistrate of Changle, and was again recommended for extraordinary promotion of ruler-like men.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the forthright remonstrance examination, was posted as magistrate of Changle, and was again recommended for extraordinary promotion.

sentences.zh: 方說輔政，故召為秘書正字，擢通事舍人、駕部員外郎。

translations.literal: Just as Yue was assisting in government, Han was therefore summoned as proofreader of the Secretariat and promoted to Palace Gate Commandant and Vice Director of the Transport Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: While Yue was assisting in government, Han was summoned as proofreader of the secretariat and promoted to palace gate commandant and vice director of the transport bureau.

sentences.zh: 家畜聲伎，目使頤令，自視王侯，人莫不惡之。

translations.literal: He kept singers and dancers at home, ordering servants with a glance and commanding with his chin, viewing himself as equal to kings and marquises — no one did not detest him.
translations.idiomatic: He kept singers and dancers at home, commanding servants with a glance, comporting himself like a prince — everyone despised him.

sentences.zh: 說罷宰相，翰出為汝州長史，徙仙州別駕。

translations.literal: When Yue left the chief ministership, Han was sent out as chief administrator of Ruzhou and transferred to vice prefect of Xianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue left office, Han was sent out as chief administrator of Ruzhou and then transferred to vice prefect of Xianzhou.

sentences.zh: 日與才士豪俠飲樂游畋，伐鼓窮歡，坐貶道州司馬，卒。

translations.literal: Day after day he drank, made merry, hunted, and roamed with talented men and bold heroes, beating drums in unrestrained revelry; on account of this he was demoted to vice prefect of Daozhou and died.
translations.idiomatic: Day after day he drank, hunted, and roamed with talented men and bold spirits, beating drums in unrestrained revelry — for which he was demoted to vice prefect of Daozhou, where he died.

sentences.zh: 孫逖孫逖，博州武水人。

translations.literal: Sun Su. Sun Su was a native of Wushui in Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Su was from Wushui in Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 後魏光祿大夫惠蔚，其先也。

translations.literal: Huiwei, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness of Northern Wei, was his ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestor was Huiwei, grand master for splendid happiness of Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 祖希壯，為韓王府典簽，四世傳一子，故無近屬。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xizhuang served as registrar of the Prince of Han's household; for four generations only one son was transmitted in each, so there were no close relatives.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xizhuang had served as registrar to the Prince of Han; for four generations each line produced only one son, so he had no close kin.

sentences.zh: 父嘉之，少孤，依外家，客涉、鞏間。

translations.literal: His father Jiazhi, orphaned young, relied on his mother's family and lived as a guest between She and Gong.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jiazhi, orphaned early, lived with his mother's family as a guest between She and Gong.

sentences.zh: 垂拱初，詣洛陽獻書，不報。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Chuigong era, he went to Luoyang to present a book; there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Chuigong era he went to Luoyang to present a book; it went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 第進士，終襄邑令。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and ended his career as magistrate of Xiangyi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and ended his career as magistrate of Xiangyi.

sentences.zh: 逖幼有文，屬思警敏。

translations.literal: Su from youth had literary talent; his composing thoughts were alert and quick.
translations.idiomatic: Su showed literary talent from youth; his mind was quick and his compositions alert.

sentences.zh: 年十五，見雍州長史崔日用，令賦土火爐，援筆成篇，理趣不凡，日用駭歎，遂與定交。

translations.literal: At age fifteen he met Chief Administrator Cui Riyong of Yongzhou, who had him compose a piece on an earthen brazier; taking up the brush he finished the piece — its reasoning and interest were extraordinary; Riyong was astonished and sighed, and thereafter they formed a firm friendship.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he met Yongzhou chief administrator Cui Riyong, who asked him to compose on an earthen brazier; he wrote the piece at a stroke with extraordinary insight — Riyong was astonished and they became close friends.

sentences.zh: 舉手筆俊拔、哲人奇士、隱淪屠釣及文藻宏麗等科。

translations.literal: He passed the examinations for outstanding brushwork, sage-like extraordinary men, recluses and fishermen, and magnificent literary adornment.
translations.idiomatic: He passed examinations for outstanding brushwork, sage-like extraordinary men, recluses and fishermen, and magnificent literary adornment.

sentences.zh: 開元十年，又舉賢良方正。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Kaiyuan, he again passed the examination for worthy and upright men.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 10 he also passed the examination for worthy and upright men.

sentences.zh: 玄宗禦洛城門引見，命戶部郎中蘇晉等第其文異等，擢左拾遺。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong received him in audience at the Luoyang city gate, ordered Director Su Jin of the Ministry of Revenue and others to rank his writing in a special grade, and promoted him to Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong received him in audience at the Luoyang city gate, had Su Jin and others rank his writing in the highest grade, and promoted him to left reminder.

sentences.zh: 張說命子均、垍往拜之。

translations.literal: Zhang Yue ordered his sons Jun and Ji to go pay their respects to him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue sent his sons Jun and Ji to pay their respects.

sentences.zh: 李邕負才，自陳州入計，裒其文示逖。

translations.literal: Li Yong, relying on his talent, coming from Chenzhou for the annual review, gathered his writings and showed them to Su.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yong, confident in his talent, came from Chenzhou for his annual account and showed Su a collection of his writings.

sentences.zh: 李暠鎮太原，表置幕府。

translations.literal: Li Hao governed Taiyuan and memorialized to appoint Su to his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hao, military commissioner of Taiyuan, memorialized to appoint Su to his staff.

sentences.zh: 以起居舍人入為集賢院脩撰。

translations.literal: As Attendant of Imperial Movements he entered to serve as compiler at the Jixian Academy.
translations.idiomatic: As attendant on imperial movements he entered the Jixian Academy as a compiler.

sentences.zh: 時海內少事，帝賜群臣十日一燕，宰相蕭嵩會百官賦《天成》、《玄澤》、《維南有山》、《楊之華》、《三月》、《英英有蘭》、《和風》、《嘉木》等詩八篇，繼《雅》、《頌》體，使逖序所以然。

translations.literal: At that time within the seas there were few affairs; the emperor granted the ministers a banquet every ten days; Chief Minister Xiao Song gathered the officials to compose eight poems — Completion of Heaven, Mysterious Marsh, There Is a Mountain to the South, The Flowering Poplar, Third Month, Luxuriant Are the Orchids, Harmonious Wind, and Fine Trees — continuing the style of the Major and Minor Odes, and had Su compose a preface explaining the reasons.
translations.idiomatic: With few affairs at home, the emperor granted ministers a banquet every ten days; chief minister Xiao Song had officials compose eight poems in the style of the Major and Minor Odes — Completion of Heaven, Mysterious Marsh, and six others — and had Su write a preface explaining their purpose.

sentences.zh: 改考功員外郎，取顏真卿、李華、蕭穎士、趙驊等，皆海內有名士。

translations.literal: He was changed to Vice Director of the Examination Bureau and selected Yan Zhenqing, Li Hua, Xiao Yingshi, Zhao Hua, and others — all renowned men within the seas.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice director of the examination bureau and selected Yan Zhenqing, Li Hua, Xiao Yingshi, Zhao Hua, and others — all celebrated men of the realm.

sentences.zh: 俄遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to drafter in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 是時，嘉之且八十，猶為令，逖求降外官，增父秩。

translations.literal: At that time Jiazhi was nearly eighty and still served as magistrate; Su requested demotion to an outer office to increase his father's rank.
translations.idiomatic: Jiazhi was nearly eighty and still serving as a magistrate; Su asked to accept a lower outer post so his father's rank might be raised.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納，拜嘉之宋州司馬，聽致仕。

translations.literal: The emperor commended and accepted this, appointing Jiazhi Vice Prefect of Songzhou and permitting him to retire.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved, appointing Jiazhi vice prefect of Songzhou and permitting him to retire.

sentences.zh: 父喪闋，復拜舍人。

translations.literal: When mourning for his father ended, he was again appointed drafter.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended he was again made a drafter.

sentences.zh: 開元間，蘇頲、齊浣、蘇晉、賈曾、韓休、許景先及逖典詔誥，為代言最，而逖尤精密，張九齡視其草，欲易一字，卒不能也。

translations.literal: During the Kaiyuan era, Su Ting, Qi Huan, Su Jin, Jia Zeng, Han Xiu, Xu Jingxian, and Su presided over edicts and proclamations as the foremost drafters on behalf of the throne; Su was especially precise — Zhang Jiuling looked at his draft, wished to change a single character, and in the end could not.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaiyuan era Su Ting, Qi Huan, Su Jin, Jia Zeng, Han Xiu, Xu Jingxian, and Su were the foremost drafters of imperial edicts; Su was especially precise — Zhang Jiuling read his draft, wished to change a single word, and could not.

sentences.zh: 居職八年，判刑部侍郎，以病風乞解，徙太子左庶子，遂綿廢累年，徙少詹事。

translations.literal: After eight years in office he was judged for Vice Minister of the Ministry of Justice; because of wind illness he requested release, was transferred to Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent, then was disabled for many years in succession, and was transferred to Junior Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: After eight years he was considered for vice minister of justice; stricken with paralysis he asked to be relieved, was made left mentor to the crown prince, remained disabled for years, and was transferred to junior mentor.

sentences.zh: 上元中卒，贈尚書右僕射，諡曰文。

translations.literal: He died during the Shangyuan era and was posthumously granted Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; his posthumous title was Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the Shangyuan era and was posthumously made right vice director of the department of state affairs, with the posthumous title Wen.

sentences.zh: 諸子成最知名。

translations.literal: Among all the sons, Cheng was the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Of all the sons, Cheng was the best known.

sentences.zh: 子 成成，字思退，推廕仕累洛陽、長安令。

translations.literal: His son Cheng, styled Situo, entered office by hereditary privilege and successively served as magistrate of Luoyang and Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: His son Cheng, courtesy name Situo, entered office through hereditary privilege and served in turn as magistrate of Luoyang and Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 兄宿為華州刺史，因悸病喑，成請告往視，不待報輒行，代宗嘉其悌，不責也。

translations.literal: When his elder brother Su was governor of Hua Prefecture and became mute from palpitation illness, Cheng requested leave to go and see him; without waiting for approval he set out. Emperor Daizong praised his filial piety and did not hold him accountable.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Su was governor of Hua Prefecture when he fell mute from a nervous disorder; Cheng requested leave to visit him and departed without waiting for approval. Emperor Daizong commended his filial devotion and did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 稍遷倉部郎中、京兆少尹。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Bureau Director in the Ministry of Revenue and Junior Assistant Administrator of the Capital Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to bureau director in the ministry of revenue and junior assistant administrator of the capital prefecture.

sentences.zh: 為信州刺史，歲大旱，發倉以賤直售民，故饑而不亡。

translations.literal: As prefect of Xinzhou, in a year of great drought he opened the granaries and sold grain to the people at low prices, so that though hungry they did not perish.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Xin Prefecture, during a severe drought he opened the granaries and sold grain cheaply to the people, so that though they went hungry none perished.

sentences.zh: 再期增戶五千，詔書褒美。

translations.literal: Within two terms the registered households increased by five thousand, and an imperial edict commended him.
translations.idiomatic: Over two terms of office the population rose by five thousand households, and an imperial edict praised his achievement.

sentences.zh: 徙蘇州，改桂管觀察使，卒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Suzhou, then made Military Commissioner of the Guiguan Circuit, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Suzhou, made military commissioner of the Guiguan circuit, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 成通經術，奏議據正。

translations.literal: Cheng was versed in the classics and in memorials and proposals relied on solid principles.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was steeped in the classics, and his memorials and proposals were grounded in principle.

sentences.zh: 嘗有期喪，吊者至，成不易縗而見。

translations.literal: Once during a period of mourning, when mourners arrived Cheng did not change out of his hempen sackcloth to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while in mourning on a fixed schedule, when callers came to pay condolences Cheng received them without changing out of his hempen mourning garments.

sentences.zh: 客疑之，請故，答曰：「縗者，古居喪常服，去之則廢喪也。

translations.literal: A visitor was puzzled and asked the reason; he replied: "The sackcloth is the customary garb for dwelling in mourning in antiquity — to remove it is to abandon the mourning."
translations.idiomatic: A guest was puzzled and asked why; he answered, "Sackcloth is the traditional garment for living in mourning — to take it off is to abandon mourning."

sentences.zh: 今而巾襆，失矣。

translations.literal: Now to wear a headcloth and kerchief — that is a lapse.
translations.idiomatic: To appear now in a turban and kerchief would be wrong.

sentences.zh: 」子公器，亦至邕管經略使。

translations.literal: His son Gongqi also rose to become Commissioner of the Yongguan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gongqi also rose to commissioner of the Yongguan circuit.

sentences.zh: 曾孫 簡公器子簡，字樞中。

translations.literal: His great-grandson Jian, son of Gongqi, styled Shuzhong.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandson Jian, Gongqi's son, courtesy name Shuzhong.

sentences.zh: 元和初，登進士第，辟鎮國、荊南幕府。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuanhe era he passed the jinshi examination and was recruited to the staffs of the Zhenguo and Jingnan commands.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Yuanhe era he passed the jinshi examination and joined the staffs of the Zhenguo and Jingnan commands.

sentences.zh: 累遷左司、吏部二郎中，繇諫議大夫知制誥，進中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Left Secretary and to both second bureau directors of the Ministry of Personnel, then from Supervising Censor to Controller of Edicts, and advanced to Drafting Secretary in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to left secretary and second bureau director in both personnel offices, then from supervising censor to controller of edicts, and was promoted to drafting secretary in the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 初，逖掌誥，至代宗時，宿又居職，逮簡凡三世。

translations.literal: At first Su presided over proclamations; by the time of Emperor Daizong, Su again held the office — down to Jian it was three generations in all.
translations.idiomatic: Su had first held the post of proclamation drafter; by Emperor Daizong's reign Su again held the office — from Su down to Jian, three generations in all.

sentences.zh: 會昌初，遷尚書左丞，建言：

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huichang he was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and submitted a proposal:
translations.idiomatic: In the early Huichang era he was made left vice director of the department of state affairs and submitted a proposal:

sentences.zh: 班位以品秩為等差，今官兼台省，位置遷誤，不可為法。

translations.literal: Court seating follows official rank and grade as gradations; now officials jointly hold posts in the censorate and secretariat, and their seats are wrongly assigned — this cannot serve as precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Court precedence follows rank and grade; when officials concurrently hold posts in the censorate and secretariat, their seating is wrongly assigned and cannot serve as precedent.

sentences.zh: 元和元年，御史台白奏，常參官兼大夫、中丞者，視檢校官，居本品同類官上。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanhe the Censorate reported that regular attendees who concurrently held Grand Counselor or Vice Censor-in-Chief were regarded as acting officials and seated above others of their own rank and kind.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe 1 the censorate reported that regular attendees holding grand counselor or vice censor-in-chief concurrently were treated as acting appointees and seated above others of the same rank.

sentences.zh: 其後侍郎兼大夫者，皆在左、右丞上。

translations.literal: Thereafter vice ministers who concurrently held Grand Counselor all sat above the left and right vice directors.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter vice ministers concurrently holding grand counselor all sat above the left and right vice directors.

sentences.zh: 當時侍郎兼大夫少，唯京兆尹兼之。

translations.literal: At the time few vice ministers concurrently held Grand Counselor; only the Administrator of the Capital Prefecture did.
translations.idiomatic: At the time few vice ministers held the grand counselor title concurrently; only the capital prefect did.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹從三品，今位乃在本品同類官從三品卿、監上，太常、宗正卿正三品下。

translations.literal: The Administrator of the Capital Prefecture was third rank, lower grade; now his seat was above fellow third rank, lower grade directors and supervisors of his own rank, though the Directors of Ceremonial and of the Imperial Clan were third rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: The capital prefect was third rank, lower grade, yet now sat above fellow third-rank, lower-grade directors and supervisors, though directors of ceremonial and of the imperial clan were third rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 左丞乃正四品上，戶部侍郎正四品下，今戶部侍郎兼大夫當在本品同類正四品下，諸曹侍郎上，不宜居正四品丞、郎上。

translations.literal: The Left Vice Director was fourth rank, upper grade; the Vice Minister of Revenue was fourth rank, lower grade — now a Vice Minister of Revenue who concurrently held Grand Counselor should be among fellow fourth rank, lower grade officials above the various bureau vice ministers, and should not sit above fourth rank directors and section chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: The left vice director was fourth rank, upper grade; the vice minister of revenue was fourth rank, lower grade — a vice minister of revenue holding grand counselor concurrently should rank among fourth-rank, lower-grade officials above the various bureau vice ministers, and should not sit above fourth-rank directors and section chiefs.

sentences.zh: 又右丞正四品下，吏部侍郎正四品上，今吏部侍郎位右丞之下。

translations.literal: Further, the Right Vice Director was fourth rank, lower grade; the Vice Minister of Personnel was fourth rank, upper grade — now the Vice Minister of Personnel sat below the Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: The right vice director was fourth rank, lower grade; the vice minister of personnel was fourth rank, upper grade — yet the vice minister of personnel now sat below the right vice director.

sentences.zh: 蓋以丞有繩轄之重，雖吏部品高，猶居其下，然則戶部侍郎雖兼大夫，安得居其上哉？

translations.literal: This was because the vice director had the weight of discipline and control — though the Personnel Ministry's rank was higher, he still sat below. Then how could the Vice Minister of Revenue, though concurrently Grand Counselor, sit above him?
translations.idiomatic: This was because the vice director's role carried disciplinary authority — though personnel outranked him in grade, he still sat above — so how could the vice minister of revenue, even as grand counselor, sit above him?

sentences.zh: 今散官自將仕郎至開府、特進，每品正、從有上中下，名級各異，則正從上下不得謂之同品。

translations.literal: Now among honorary offices from Court Gentleman for Meritorious Achievement through Special Grand Mentor, each rank has upper, middle, and lower grades for both regular and adjunct status — the names and grades all differ; regular and adjunct, upper and lower cannot be called the same rank.
translations.idiomatic: Among honorary ranks from court gentleman for meritorious achievement through special grand mentor, each grade has upper, middle, and lower levels in both regular and adjunct status — titles and levels all differ, so regular and adjunct, upper and lower, cannot be treated as the same rank.

sentences.zh: 京兆、河南司錄及諸府州錄事參軍事皆操紀律，正諸曹，與尚書省左、右丞紀綱六曹略等，假使諸曹掾因功勞加台省官，安得位在司錄、錄事參軍上？

translations.literal: The chief clerks of the Capital and Henan prefectures and the recording secretaries of all prefectures and districts hold the rules of discipline and regulate all bureaus — comparable to the left and right vice directors who govern the six bureaus of the Department of State Affairs. Even if a bureau assistant gained a censorate or secretariat post through merit, how could he rank above the chief clerk and recording secretary?
translations.idiomatic: The chief clerks of the capital and Henan prefectures and the recording secretaries of all prefectures hold disciplinary authority and regulate the bureaus — comparable to the left and right vice directors governing the six ministries — so even if a bureau aide earned a concurrent censorate or secretariat post through merit, how could he rank above chief clerk or recording secretary?

sentences.zh: 且左丞糾射八坐，主省內禁令、宗廟祠祭事，御史不當，得彈奏之，良以台官所奏，拘牽成例，不揣事之輕重。

translations.literal: Moreover the Left Vice Director examines and impeaches the eight chief ministers, supervises inner prohibitions and ancestral temple sacrifices, and when censors were improper could impeach them — for censorate memorials were constrained by precedent and did not weigh the gravity of matters.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the left vice director censures the chief ministers, oversees court prohibitions and ancestral sacrifices, and could impeach censors who overstepped — because censorate reports were bound by precedent without weighing the seriousness of each case.

sentences.zh: 使理可循，雖無往比，自宜行之。

translations.literal: Where principle can be followed, even without past parallel, it should be implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Where principle applies, it should be adopted even without a precedent.

sentences.zh: 否者，號曰舊章，正可改也。

translations.literal: Otherwise what is called old regulation is precisely what should be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise what is called established custom is exactly what ought to be revised.

sentences.zh: 武宗詔兩省官詳議，皆從簡請。

translations.literal: Emperor Wuzong ordered the officials of both secretariats to discuss in detail, and all agreed with Jian's request.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wuzong ordered officials of both secretariates to deliberate; all approved Jian's proposal.

sentences.zh: 曆河中、興元、宣武節度使，檢校尚書右僕射、東都留守。

translations.literal: He served in succession as military commissioner of Hedong, Xingyuan, and Xuanwu, with the acting title Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and as Keeper of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as military commissioner of Hedong, Xingyuan, and Xuanwu, with the acting title right vice director of the department of state affairs, and as keeper of the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 而弟范亦為淄青節度使，世推顯家。

translations.literal: Meanwhile his younger brother Fan also became military commissioner of Ziqing — the world acclaimed them a prominent family.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Fan also became military commissioner of Ziqing; the family was renowned for its eminence.

sentences.zh: 李白李白，字太白，興聖皇帝九世孫。

translations.literal: Li Bai, styled Taibai, was a ninth-generation descendant of Emperor Xingsheng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bai, courtesy name Taibai, was ninth-generation descendant of Emperor Xingsheng.

sentences.zh: 其先隋末以罪徙西域，神龍初，遁還，客巴西。

translations.literal: His forebears were banished to the Western Regions for a crime at the end of Sui; at the beginning of Shenlong they fled back and settled as guests in Baxi.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors were exiled to the western regions for a crime at the end of Sui; at the start of Shenlong they slipped back and lived as guests in Baxi.

sentences.zh: 白之生，母夢長庚星，因以命之。

translations.literal: At Bai's birth his mother dreamed of the Chang'geng star, and so named him after it.
translations.idiomatic: When Bai was born his mother dreamed of the planet Venus and named him for it.

sentences.zh: 十歲通詩書，既長，隱岷山。

translations.literal: At ten he mastered poetry and books; when grown he lived in seclusion on Mount Min.
translations.idiomatic: At ten he mastered the classics; grown, he withdrew to Mount Min.

sentences.zh: 州舉有道，不應。

translations.literal: The prefecture recommended him for the "Way and Integrity" candidacy; he did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture nominated him for the "Way and Integrity" candidacy; he declined.

sentences.zh: 蘇頲為益州長史，見白異之，曰：「是子天才英特，少益以學，可比相如。

translations.literal: When Su Ting was chief secretary of Yizhou he saw Bai and thought him extraordinary, saying: "This boy's talent is singularly gifted — with a little more learning he could rival Xiangru."
translations.idiomatic: When Su Ting was chief secretary of Yizhou he noticed Bai and said, "This boy's genius is extraordinary — with a little more study he could rival Sima Xiangru."

sentences.zh: 」然喜縱橫術，擊劍，為任俠，輕財重施。

translations.literal: Yet he loved strategists' arts and swordplay, acted as a chivalrous knight, and was generous with money.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he loved political strategy, swordsmanship, and the life of a knight-errant, giving freely of his wealth.

sentences.zh: 更客任城，與孔巢父、韓准、裴政、張叔明、陶沔居徂徠山，日沈飲，號「竹溪六逸」。

translations.literal: Later he sojourned at Rencheng and with Kong Chaofu, Han Zhun, Pei Zheng, Zhang Shuming, and Tao Mian lived on Mount Zou'e, drinking deep each day — they were called the "Six Recluses of Bamboo Creek."
translations.idiomatic: Later he stayed at Rencheng, and with Kong Chaofu, Han Zhun, Pei Zheng, Zhang Shuming, and Tao Mian lived on Mount Zou'e, drinking all day — they were called the "Six Recluses of Bamboo Creek."

sentences.zh: 天寶初，南入會稽，與吳筠善，筠被召，故白亦至長安。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he went south to Kuaiji, befriended Wu Yun; when Yun was summoned, Bai also came to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianbao era he went south to Kuaiji and befriended Wu Yun; when Yun was summoned to court, Bai went to Chang'an as well.

sentences.zh: 往見賀知章，知章見其文，歎曰：「子，謫仙人也！

translations.literal: He went to see He Zhizhang; Zhizhang read his writings and exclaimed: "You are a banished immortal!"
translations.idiomatic: He visited He Zhizhang, who read his writings and cried, "You are a banished immortal!"

sentences.zh: 」言于玄宗，召見金鑾殿，論當世事，奏頌一篇。

translations.literal: He spoke to Emperor Xuanzong; Bai was summoned to an audience at the Hall of Golden Bells, discussed affairs of the day, and presented a eulogy.
translations.idiomatic: He told Emperor Xuanzong, who summoned Bai to the Hall of Golden Bells; Bai discussed current affairs and presented a eulogy.

sentences.zh: 帝賜食，親為調羹，有詔供奉翰林。

translations.literal: The emperor bestowed food and personally seasoned the broth; an edict appointed him to the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave him food and personally mixed his broth; an edict appointed him to the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 白猶與飲徒醉於市。

translations.literal: Bai still went about the marketplace drunk with his drinking companions.
translations.idiomatic: Bai still caroused drunk through the marketplace with his drinking companions.

sentences.zh: 帝坐沈香亭子，意有所感，欲得白為樂章；

translations.literal: The emperor sat in the Pavilion of Aloes and Sandalwood, stirred by some feeling, and wished to have Bai compose a song text;
translations.idiomatic: Seated in the Pavilion of Aloes and Sandalwood, the emperor was moved and wanted Bai to write lyrics;

sentences.zh: 召入，而白已醉，左右以水靧面，稍解，援筆成文，婉麗精切無留思。

translations.literal: When summoned, Bai was already drunk; attendants splashed water on his face and when he sobered slightly he took up the brush and completed the text — elegant, refined, precise, without hesitation.
translations.idiomatic: When summoned Bai was already drunk; attendants splashed water on his face, and once he recovered slightly he took up the brush and finished at once — graceful, refined, precise, without a moment's delay.

sentences.zh: 帝愛其才，數宴見。

translations.literal: The emperor loved his talent and repeatedly summoned him to banquets.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired his talent and repeatedly invited him to court banquets.

sentences.zh: 白嘗侍帝，醉，使高力士脫靴。

translations.literal: Once while attending the emperor, Bai was drunk and ordered Gao Lishi to remove his boots.
translations.idiomatic: Once while attending the emperor Bai was drunk and ordered Gao Lishi to remove his boots.

sentences.zh: 力士素貴，恥之，擿其詩以激楊貴妃，帝欲官白，妃輒沮止。

translations.literal: Lishi was by nature honored and took this as shame; he picked out lines from Bai's poems to provoke Yang Guifei — when the emperor wished to grant Bai office, the consort always obstructed and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: Lishi, a man of high standing, took this as humiliation; he found fault in Bai's poems to anger Yang Guifei — whenever the emperor wished to grant Bai office, the consort blocked it.

sentences.zh: 白自知不為親近所容，益驁放不自脩，與知章、李適之、汝陽王璡、崔宗之、蘇晉、張旭、焦遂為「酒八仙人」。

translations.literal: Bai knew he was not tolerated by those close to the throne and became all the more proud and unrestrained; with Zhizhang, Li Shizhi, Prince of Ruyang Li Jin, Cui Zongzhi, Su Jin, Zhang Xu, and Jiao Su he was called the "Eight Immortals of the Wine Cup."
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he was unwelcome at court, Bai grew ever more unrestrained; with Zhizhang, Li Shizhi, Prince of Ruyang Li Jin, Cui Zongzhi, Su Jin, Zhang Xu, and Jiao Su he was called the "Eight Immortals of the Wine Cup."

sentences.zh: 懇求還山，帝賜金放還。

translations.literal: He earnestly requested to return to the mountains; the emperor bestowed gold and released him.
translations.idiomatic: He begged to return to the mountains; the emperor gave him gold and let him go.

sentences.zh: 白浮游四方，嘗乘舟與崔宗之自採石至金陵，著宮錦袍坐舟中，旁若無人。

translations.literal: Bai wandered the four directions; once he took a boat with Cui Zongzhi from Caishi to Jinling, wearing a palace brocade robe and sitting in the boat as if no one else were present.
translations.idiomatic: Bai wandered everywhere; once he sailed with Cui Zongzhi from Caishi to Jinling in a palace brocade robe, seated in the boat as if alone in the world.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，轉側宿松、匡廬間，永王璘辟為府僚佐。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, he moved about between Susong and Mount Lushan; Prince of Yong Li Lin recruited him as staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled he wandered between Susong and Mount Lu; Prince of Yong Li Lin took him on as a staff officer.

sentences.zh: 璘起兵，逃還彭澤，璘敗，當誅。

translations.literal: When Lin raised troops, Bai fled back to Pengze; when Lin was defeated Bai was liable to execution.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin rose in arms Bai fled to Pengze; when Lin was defeated Bai faced execution.

sentences.zh: 初，白遊并州，見郭子儀，奇之。

translations.literal: Earlier Bai had traveled to Bing Prefecture, seen Guo Ziyi, and thought him extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while traveling in Bing Prefecture, Bai met Guo Ziyi and was impressed.

sentences.zh: 子儀嘗犯法，白為救免。

translations.literal: Ziyi once violated the law and Bai had him rescued and pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: When Ziyi once broke the law, Bai had him spared.

sentences.zh: 至是子儀請解官以贖，有詔長流夜郎。

translations.literal: At this time Ziyi requested to resign office to redeem him; an edict banished Bai far to Yelang.
translations.idiomatic: Now Ziyi offered to resign his office to save him; an edict exiled Bai to distant Yelang.

sentences.zh: 會赦，還尋陽，坐事下獄。

translations.literal: He met an amnesty, returned to Xunyang, and was imprisoned for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty brought him back to Xunyang, where he was jailed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 時宋若思將吳兵三千赴河南，道尋陽，釋囚辟為參謀，未幾辭職。

translations.literal: At the time Song Ruosi was leading three thousand Wu troops to Henan; passing Xunyang he released the prisoner and recruited him as strategic adviser; before long Bai resigned.
translations.idiomatic: Song Ruosi was then leading three thousand Wu troops to Henan; passing Xunyang he freed Bai and made him his adviser, but Bai soon resigned.

sentences.zh: 李陽冰為當塗令，白依之。

translations.literal: Li Yangbing was magistrate of Dangtu and Bai relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yangbing was magistrate of Dangtu, and Bai stayed with him.

sentences.zh: 代宗立，以左拾遺召，而白已卒，年六十餘。

translations.literal: When Emperor Daizong ascended, Bai was summoned as Left Remonstrance Officer, but he had already died, aged over sixty.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Daizong ascended, Bai was recalled as left remonstrance officer, but he had already died at over sixty.

sentences.zh: 白晚好黃老，度牛渚磯至姑孰，悅謝家青山，欲終焉。

translations.literal: In his later years Bai favored Daoism; crossing Ox Rock Ford to reach Gushu he delighted in the Green Mountain of the Xie family and wished to end his days there.
translations.idiomatic: In later years Bai turned to Daoism; crossing Ox-Rock Ford to Gushu he fell in love with the Xie family's Green Mountain and wished to end his days there.

sentences.zh: 及卒，葬東麓。

translations.literal: When he died he was buried on the eastern slope.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was buried on the eastern slope.

sentences.zh: 元和末，宣歙觀察使范傳正祭其塚，禁樵採。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanhe, Military Commissioner of the Xuanshe Circuit Fan Chuanzheng sacrificed at his tomb and forbade woodcutting.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuanhe era Fan Chuanzheng, military commissioner of the Xuanshe circuit, sacrificed at his tomb and forbade logging.

sentences.zh: 訪後裔，惟二孫女嫁為民妻，進止仍有風範，因泣曰：「先祖志在青山，頃葬東麓，非本意。

translations.literal: Inquiring for descendants he found only two granddaughters married to commoners; their bearing still showed refinement — he wept and said: "Our ancestor's wish was for Green Mountain; he was recently buried on the eastern slope — not his true intent."
translations.idiomatic: Seeking descendants he found only two granddaughters married to commoners; their bearing still showed dignity — he wept and said, "Our ancestor wished to rest on Green Mountain; the recent burial on the eastern slope was not his intent."

sentences.zh: 」傳正為改葬，立二碑焉。

translations.literal: Chuanzheng had him reburied and erected two steles.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanzheng had him reburied and set up two steles.

sentences.zh: 告二女，將改妻士族，辭以孤窮失身，命也，不願更嫁。

translations.literal: He told the two daughters he would remarry them to gentry families; they declined, saying that in their poverty and isolation they had lost their status — it was fate — and they did not wish to marry again.
translations.idiomatic: He told the granddaughters he would marry them into gentry families; they refused, saying that in poverty and isolation they had been reduced to common wives — it was fate — and they did not wish to remarry.

sentences.zh: 傳正嘉歎，復其夫徭役。

translations.literal: Chuanzheng praised and sighed and restored their husbands' labor duties.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanzheng admired them and remitted their husbands' corvée obligations.

sentences.zh: 文宗時，詔以白歌詩、裴旻劍舞、張旭草書為「三絕」。

translations.literal: During Emperor Wenzong's reign an edict named Bai's song-poetry, Pei Min's sword dance, and Zhang Xu's cursive script as the "Three Unsurpassed Arts."
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Wenzong's reign an edict named Bai's poetry, Pei Min's sword dance, and Zhang Xu's cursive script the "Three Unsurpassed Arts."

sentences.zh: 附 張旭旭，蘇州吳人。

translations.literal: Appendix — Zhang Xu, styled Bo, was a native of Wu in Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Zhang Xu, courtesy name Bo, was from Wu in Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 嗜酒，每大醉，呼叫狂走，乃下筆，或以頭濡墨而書，既醒自視，以為神，不可復得也，世呼「張顛」。

translations.literal: He loved wine; each time he drank deep he would shout and run wildly, then put brush to paper — sometimes dipping his head in ink to write; when sober he looked at the work and thought it divine, unable to reproduce it — the world called him "Zhang the Mad."
translations.idiomatic: He loved wine; drunk he shouted and ran wild before writing — sometimes dipping his head in ink — and when sober marveled at work he could never replicate; he was called "Zhang the Mad."

sentences.zh: 初，仕為常熟尉，有老人陳牒求判，宿昔又來，旭怒其煩，責之。

translations.literal: At first he served as magistrate of Changshu; an old man submitted a petition seeking judgment, and after a night came again — Xu was angry at the annoyance and scolded him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in his career he was magistrate of Changshu; an old man brought a petition for judgment, and returned the next night — Xu, annoyed, scolded him.

sentences.zh: 老人曰：「觀公筆奇妙，欲以藏家爾。

translations.literal: The old man said: "Seeing your brushwork is marvelous, I wished to keep it in my family."
translations.idiomatic: The old man said, "Seeing your brushwork's marvel, I wished to keep it in my family."

sentences.zh: 」旭因問所藏，盡出其父書，旭視之，天下奇筆也，自是盡其法。

translations.literal: Xu then asked what he kept; the man produced all his father's writings — Xu looked at them and they were matchless brushwork under heaven; from then on he mastered the full art.
translations.idiomatic: Xu asked what he kept; the man produced his father's entire collection — Xu saw matchless brushwork and from then mastered the art completely.

sentences.zh: 旭自言，始見公主擔夫爭道，又聞鼓吹，而得筆法意，觀倡公孫舞《劍器》，得其神。

translations.literal: Xu himself said he first gained the idea of brush method from watching the bearers of a princess jostling for the road and hearing the ceremonial music; from watching the performer Gongsun dance "Sword Brandish" he grasped its spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Xu said he first caught the spirit of the brush watching a princess's bearers jostling on the road and hearing ceremonial music; watching the courtesan Gongsun dance "Sword Brandish" he grasped its essence.

sentences.zh: 後人論書，歐、虞、褚、陸皆有異論，至旭，無非短者。

translations.literal: Later commentators on calligraphy all had differing views of Ouyang, Yu, Chu, and Lu — as for Xu, none had anything but praise.
translations.idiomatic: Later critics of calligraphy disputed over Ouyang, Yu, Chu, and Lu — but on Xu none had a word of criticism.

sentences.zh: 傳其法，惟崔邈、顏真卿云。

translations.literal: Those who transmitted his method were only Cui Miao and Yan Zhenqing, they say.
translations.idiomatic: Only Cui Miao and Yan Zhenqing, it is said, transmitted his method.

sentences.zh: 附 裴旻旻嘗與幽州都督孫佺北伐，為奚所圍，旻舞刀立馬上，矢四集，皆迎刀而斷，奚大驚引去。

translations.literal: Appendix — Pei Min: Min once joined the Northern Expedition of Sun Qian, military commissioner of Youzhou; surrounded by the Xi, Min danced his blade standing on horseback — four arrows came at once and he severed each on the blade; the Xi were greatly alarmed and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Pei Min once joined Youzhou commissioner Sun Qian's northern campaign; surrounded by the Xi, Min whirled his blade on horseback — four arrows flew at him and he cut each aside; the Xi fled in alarm.

sentences.zh: 後以龍華軍使守北平。

translations.literal: Later as commander of Longhua Army he garrisoned Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as commander of the Longhua army, he garrisoned Beiping.

sentences.zh: 北平多虎，旻善射，一日得虎三十一，休山下。

translations.literal: Beiping had many tigers; Min was skilled at archery — in one day he took thirty-one tigers, resting beneath the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Beiping teemed with tigers; Min was an expert archer — one day he killed thirty-one at the foot of the mountain.

sentences.zh: 有老父曰：「此彪也。

translations.literal: An old man said: "Those were cubs."
translations.idiomatic: An old man said, "Those were cubs."

sentences.zh: 稍北，有真虎，使將軍遇之，且敗。

translations.literal: Farther north are real tigers — should the general meet them, he will be defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Farther north are real tigers — if the general meets them, he will lose.

sentences.zh: 」旻不信，怒馬趨之。

translations.literal: Min did not believe it and drove his horse angrily forward.
translations.idiomatic: Min did not believe it and spurred his horse forward in anger.

sentences.zh: 有虎出叢薄中，小而猛，據地大吼，旻馬辟易，弓矢皆墮，自是不復射。

translations.literal: A tiger emerged from the thicket — small but fierce, it crouched and roared; Min's horse shied, bow and arrows fell away — from then on he never shot again.
translations.idiomatic: A small fierce tiger burst from the thicket, crouched and roared — Min's horse bolted, his bow and arrows fell — and he never hunted again.

sentences.zh: 王維王維，字摩詰。

translations.literal: Wang Wei, styled Mojie.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wei, courtesy name Mojie.

sentences.zh: 九歲知屬辭，與弟縉齊名，資孝友。

translations.literal: At nine he could compose verse; he and his younger brother Jin were equally famed; his nature was filial and friendly.
translations.idiomatic: At nine he could write polished prose; he and his younger brother Jin were equally celebrated for filial devotion and brotherly affection.

sentences.zh: 開元初，擢進士，調太樂丞，坐累為濟州司倉參軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed Vice Director of the Imperial Music Office, and through entanglement was demoted to grain-store secretary of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyuan he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed vice director of the imperial music office, and through involvement in a case was demoted to grain-store secretary of Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 張九齡執政，擢右拾遺。

translations.literal: When Zhang Jiuling held power he was promoted to Right Remonstrance Officer.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhang Jiuling he was promoted to right remonstrance officer.

sentences.zh: 歷監察御史。

translations.literal: He served as Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He served as investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 母喪，毀幾不生。

translations.literal: At his mother's death his grief nearly killed him.
translations.idiomatic: At his mother's death his grief nearly cost him his life.

sentences.zh: 服除，累遷給事中。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was promoted in succession to Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was promoted to supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，玄宗西狩，維為賊得，以藥下利，陽喑。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled Emperor Xuanzong fled west; Wei was captured by the rebels, took medicine to induce dysentery, and feigned muteness.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled and Emperor Xuanzong fled west, Wei was captured; he took purgative medicine and feigned muteness.

sentences.zh: 祿山素知其才，迎置洛陽，迫為給事中。

translations.literal: Lushan knew his talent and brought him to Luoyang, forcing him to serve as Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan knew his talent, brought him to Luoyang, and forced him to serve as supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 祿山大宴凝碧池，悉召梨園諸工合樂，諸工皆泣，維聞悲甚，賦詩悼痛。

translations.literal: Lushan gave a great banquet at Ningbi Pool and summoned all the Pear Garden musicians to perform together; all the musicians wept — hearing it Wei was deeply grieved and composed a poem of mourning and pain.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan held a great banquet at Ningbi Pool and summoned all Pear Garden musicians; they wept and Wei, hearing it, was grief-stricken and wrote a lament.

sentences.zh: 賊平，皆下獄。

translations.literal: When the rebels were suppressed all were imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebellion was crushed all were imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 或以詩聞行在，時縉位已顯，請削官贖維罪，肅宗亦自憐之，下遷太子中允。

translations.literal: Some reported his poem to the emperor's traveling court; at that time Jin's position was already prominent — he requested to reduce his own office to redeem Wei's crime; Emperor Suzong also took pity and demoted Wei to Middle Secretary to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Word of his poem reached the emperor's camp; Jin, by then eminent, asked to demote himself to redeem Wei; Emperor Suzong took pity and reduced Wei to middle secretary to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷中庶子，三遷尚書右丞。

translations.literal: After a long while he was transferred to Middle Mentor, and in three steps promoted to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In time he became middle mentor and after three promotions reached right vice director of the department of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 縉為蜀州刺史未還，維自表「己有五短，縉五長，臣在省戶，縉遠方，願歸所任官，放田里，使縉得還京師。

translations.literal: Jin was governor of Shu Prefecture and had not returned — Wei submitted a memorial himself: "I have five shortcomings, Jin five strengths; I am at the capital household, Jin is in a distant region — I wish to resign my current post and be sent to the countryside so that Jin may return to the capital."
translations.idiomatic: Jin was governor of Shu and had not returned; Wei submitted a memorial: "I have five shortcomings and Jin five strengths; I am in the capital while Jin is far away — I ask to resign my post and retire to the countryside so Jin can return to the capital."

sentences.zh: 」議者不之罪。

translations.literal: The critics did not blame him.
translations.idiomatic: The critics did not hold him at fault.

sentences.zh: 久乃召縉為左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: After a long while Jin was summoned as Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: After some time Jin was recalled as left regular attendant of the cavalry.

sentences.zh: 上元初卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: In the early Shangyuan era he died, aged sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the early Shangyuan era at sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 疾甚，縉在鳳翔，作書與別，又遺親故書數幅，停筆而化。

translations.literal: When gravely ill, with Jin at Fengxiang, he wrote a letter of farewell and also left several letters to kin and friends, then set down his brush and passed away.
translations.idiomatic: Seriously ill, with Jin at Fengxiang, he wrote a farewell letter and several letters to kin and friends, then set down his brush and died.

sentences.zh: 贈秘書監。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 維工草隸，善畫，名盛於開元、天寶間，豪英貴人虛左以迎，甯、薛諸王待若師友。

translations.literal: Wei excelled at cursive and clerical script and was skilled at painting; his fame flourished in the Kaiyuan and Tianbao eras — eminent nobles left the seat of honor to receive him, and the Princes of Ning and Xue treated him as teacher and friend.
translations.idiomatic: Wei excelled at cursive and clerical script and painting; his fame peaked in the Kaiyuan and Tianbao eras — eminent nobles left the seat of honor to receive him, and the princes of Ning and Xue treated him as teacher and friend.

sentences.zh: 畫思入神，至山水準遠，雲勢石色，繪工以為天機所到，學者不及也。

translations.literal: His painting thought penetrated the divine; in landscape he reached remoteness — cloud momentum and stone color — painters held it the work of heaven's inspiration, which students could not attain.
translations.idiomatic: His painting reached into the spirit; in landscape he achieved remoteness — cloud forms and stone hues — painters called it heaven's inspiration, beyond what students could match.

sentences.zh: 客有以《按樂圖》示者，無題識，維徐曰：「此《霓裳》第三疊最初拍也。

translations.literal: A visitor showed him "Musicians Rehearsing"; it had no inscription — Wei said slowly: "This is the initial beat of the third movement of the Rainbow Skirt and Feathered Coat."
translations.idiomatic: A visitor showed him Musicians Rehearsing without inscription; Wei said slowly, "This is the opening beat of the third movement of Rainbow Skirt and Feathered Coat."

sentences.zh: 」客未然，引工按曲，乃信。

translations.literal: The visitor was not yet convinced; musicians were brought to perform the tune, and then he believed.
translations.idiomatic: The visitor was unconvinced until musicians played the tune and proved it.

sentences.zh: 兄弟皆篤志奉佛，食不葷，衣不文彩。

translations.literal: The brothers were all devoted to Buddhism, ate no meat, and wore no patterned silks.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers were all devout Buddhists who ate no meat and wore plain cloth.

sentences.zh: 別墅在輞川，地奇勝，有華子岡、欹湖、竹裏館、柳浪、茱萸沜、辛夷塢，與裴迪遊其中，賦詩相酬為樂。

translations.literal: Their villa was at Wangchuan, a place of strange beauty, with Huazi Hillock, Slanting Lake, Bamboo Grove Lodge, Willow Waves, Dogwood Marsh, and Magnolia Bank — with Pei Di they wandered there, composing poems in mutual response for delight.
translations.idiomatic: Their villa at Wangchuan was a place of rare beauty, with Huazi Hillock, Slanting Lake, Bamboo Grove Lodge, Willow Waves, Dogwood Marsh, and Magnolia Bank — there Wei and Pei Di wandered, exchanging poems for pleasure.

sentences.zh: 喪妻不娶，孤居三十年。

translations.literal: After his wife's death he did not remarry and lived alone for thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: After his wife died he never remarried and lived alone for thirty years.

sentences.zh: 母亡，表輞川第為寺，終葬其西。

translations.literal: When his mother died he petitioned to make the Wangchuan estate a temple and was buried on its western side.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he made the Wangchuan estate a temple and was buried on its western side.

sentences.zh: 寶應中，代宗語縉曰：「朕嘗于諸王座聞維樂章，今傳幾何？

translations.literal: During the Baoying era Emperor Daizong said to Jin: "I once heard Wei's song texts among the princes — how many survive now?"
translations.idiomatic: During the Baoying era Emperor Daizong told Jin, "I once heard Wei's song texts among the princes at court — how many survive now?"

sentences.zh: 」遣中人王承華往取，縉裒集數十百篇上之。

translations.literal: He sent the eunuch Wang Chenghua to fetch them; Jin collected several hundred pieces and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the eunuch Wang Chenghua to fetch them; Jin collected several hundred pieces and presented them.

sentences.zh: 鄭虔鄭虔，鄭州滎陽人。

translations.literal: Zheng Qian, a native of Xingyang in Zheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Qian was from Xingyang in Zheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，為協律郎，集綴當世事，著書八十餘篇。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he served as Director of Music, compiled current affairs, and wrote more than eighty chapters.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianbao he served as director of music, compiled current affairs, and wrote more than eighty chapters.

sentences.zh: 有窺其稿者，上書告虔私撰國史，虔蒼黃焚之，坐謫十年。

translations.literal: Someone who had glimpsed his draft reported that Qian was privately compiling a national history; Qian in panic burned it and was demoted for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Someone who had glimpsed his draft reported that Qian was privately compiling a national history; Qian panicked and burned it, and was demoted for ten years.

sentences.zh: 還京師，玄宗愛其才，欲置左右，以不事事，更為置廣文館，以虔為博士。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital, Emperor Xuanzong loved his talent and wished to place him at his side; because he was unmanageable, he instead established the Broad Culture Academy and made Qian its erudite.
translations.idiomatic: Back in the capital, Emperor Xuanzong admired his talent and wished to keep him at court; finding him unmanageable, he established the Broad Culture Academy and made Qian its erudite.

sentences.zh: 虔聞命，不知廣文曹司何在，訴宰相，宰相曰：「上增國學，置廣文館，以居賢者，令後世言廣文博士自君始，不亦美乎？

translations.literal: When Qian received the appointment he did not know where the Broad Culture office was and complained to the chief minister, who said: "His Majesty has expanded the national academy and established the Broad Culture Academy to house men of talent — that posterity should say the Broad Culture erudite began with you — is that not fine?"
translations.idiomatic: Receiving the appointment, Qian did not know where the Broad Culture office was and complained to the chief minister, who said, "His Majesty has expanded the national academy and established the Broad Culture Academy for men of talent — that posterity should say the Broad Culture erudite began with you — is that not fine?"

sentences.zh: 」虔乃就職。

translations.literal: Qian then took up the post.
translations.idiomatic: Qian then took up the post.

sentences.zh: 久之，雨壞廡舍，有司不復修完，寓治國子館，自是遂廢。

translations.literal: After a long while rain damaged the corridors; the authorities did not repair them, and the academy was housed in the Directorate of Education — from then it was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: After a time rain damaged the corridors; the authorities did not repair them, and the academy was housed in the directorate of education — from then it lapsed.

sentences.zh: 初，虔追紬故書可志者得四十餘篇，國子司業蘇源明名其書為《會稡》。

translations.literal: At first Qian had traced old writings worth recording and obtained more than forty chapters; Su Yuanming, vice director of the national academy, named the book "Collected Records."
translations.idiomatic: Qian had traced old writings worth recording and obtained more than forty chapters; Su Yuanming, vice director of the national academy, named the book Collected Records.

sentences.zh: 虔善圖山水，好書，常苦無紙，於是慈恩寺貯柿葉數屋，遂往日取葉肄書，歲久殆遍。

translations.literal: Qian was skilled at landscape painting and loved calligraphy but often lacked paper; he stored persimmon leaves in several rooms at Cien Temple and went daily to take leaves to practice writing — over years he nearly used them all.
translations.idiomatic: Qian was skilled at landscape painting and loved calligraphy but often lacked paper; he stored persimmon leaves in several rooms at Cien Temple and went daily to practice on them — over years he nearly used them all.

sentences.zh: 嘗自寫其詩並畫以獻，帝大署其尾曰：「鄭虔三絕」。

translations.literal: He once copied his own poems and paintings to present; the emperor wrote large characters at the end: "Zheng Qian's Three Unsurpassed Arts."
translations.idiomatic: He once presented his own poems and paintings; the emperor wrote large characters at the end: "Zheng Qian's Three Unsurpassed Arts."

sentences.zh: 遷著作郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Secretary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to secretary of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，遣張通儒劫百官置東都，偽授虔水部郎中，因稱風緩，求攝市令，潛以密章達靈武。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled he sent Zhang Tongru to seize the officials and place them in the eastern capital; Qian was falsely appointed Bureau Director in the Ministry of Works, then claimed wind paralysis and sought to serve as market overseer, secretly sending a confidential memorial to Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled he sent Zhang Tongru to seize the officials for the eastern capital; Qian was falsely made bureau director in the ministry of works, then claimed wind paralysis and sought to serve as market overseer, secretly sending a confidential memorial to Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 賊平，與張通、王維並囚宣陽裏。

translations.literal: When the rebels were suppressed he was imprisoned with Zhang Tong and Wang Wei in Xuanyang Lane.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebellion was crushed he was imprisoned with Zhang Tong and Wang Wei in Xuanyang Lane.

sentences.zh: 三人者，皆善畫，崔圓使繪齋壁，虔等方悸死，即極思祈解於圓，卒免死，貶台州司戶參軍事，維止下選。

translations.literal: All three were skilled at painting; Cui Yuan had them paint the study walls — Qian and the others, fearing death, exerted all their thought to beg release from Yuan and at last escaped death, being demoted to grain-store secretary of Taizhou; Wei was only reduced in selection.
translations.idiomatic: All three were skilled at painting; Cui Yuan had them paint the study walls — terrified of death, they begged Yuan with all their might and at last escaped execution; Qian was demoted to grain-store secretary of Taizhou and Wei only reduced in selection.

sentences.zh: 後數年卒。

translations.literal: Several years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he died.

sentences.zh: 虔學長于地理，山川險易、方隅物產、兵戍眾寡無不詳。

translations.literal: Qian's learning excelled in geography — the dangers and ease of mountains and rivers, regional products, garrison strength and numbers — none was not detailed.
translations.idiomatic: Qian excelled in geography — the terrain of mountains and rivers, regional products, garrison strength — none was not detailed.

sentences.zh: 嘗為《天寶軍防錄》，言典事該。

translations.literal: He once compiled the "Tianbao Military Defense Records," treating canonical matters comprehensively.
translations.idiomatic: He once compiled the Tianbao Military Defense Records, treating canonical matters comprehensively.

sentences.zh: 諸儒服其善著書，時號「鄭廣文」。

translations.literal: The scholars admired his skill in writing; he was called "Broad Culture Zheng."
translations.idiomatic: Scholars admired his writing; he was called "Broad Culture Zheng."

sentences.zh: 在官貧約甚，澹如也。

translations.literal: In office he was extremely poor and frugal, yet tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was extremely poor and frugal, yet at peace.

sentences.zh: 杜甫嘗贈以詩曰「才名四十年，坐客寒無氈」云。

translations.literal: Du Fu once presented him a poem saying "Forty years of fame, yet guests sit in cold without felt" and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Du Fu once presented him a poem saying "Forty years of fame, yet guests sit in cold without felt" and the like.

sentences.zh: 有鄭相如者，自滄州來，師事虔，虔未之禮，間問何所業，相如曰：「聞孔子稱'繼周者百世可知'，僕亦能知之。

translations.literal: There was a Zheng Xiangru who came from Cangzhou to study under Qian; Qian did not treat him with ceremony and casually asked what he pursued — Xiangru said: "I heard Confucius say 'he who continues Zhou may be known a hundred generations hence' — I too can know this."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xiangru came from Cangzhou to study under Qian; Qian did not treat him with ceremony and asked what he pursued — Xiangru said, "I heard Confucius say 'he who continues Zhou may be known a hundred generations hence' — I too can know this."

sentences.zh: 」虔駭然，即曰：「開元盡三十年當改元，盡十五年天下亂，賊臣僭位，公當汙偽官，願守節，可以免。

translations.literal: Qian was startled and immediately said: "The Kaiyuan era will end in thirty years and the reign title will change; in fifteen years the realm will be in chaos, usurping ministers will seize the throne — you will be stained serving the false regime; if you wish to keep your integrity you may escape."
translations.idiomatic: Qian was startled and said, "The Kaiyuan era will end in thirty years and the reign title will change; in fifteen years the realm will fall into chaos, usurping ministers will seize the throne — you will be stained serving the false regime; if you wish to keep your integrity you may escape."

sentences.zh: 」虔又問：「自謂云何？

translations.literal: Qian asked again: "What of yourself?"
translations.idiomatic: Qian asked again, "What of yourself?"

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「相如有官三年，死衢州。

translations.literal: He answered: "Xiangru will hold office three years and die in Qu Prefecture."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Xiangru will hold office three years and die in Qu Prefecture."

sentences.zh: 」是年及進士第，調信安尉。

translations.literal: That year he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed assistant magistrate of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: That year he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed assistant magistrate of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 既三年，虔詢吏部，則相如果死。

translations.literal: After three years Qian inquired at the Ministry of Personnel and learned that Xiangru had indeed died.
translations.idiomatic: After three years Qian inquired at the ministry of personnel and learned that Xiangru had indeed died.

sentences.zh: 故虔念其言，終不附賊。

translations.literal: Therefore Qian kept his words in mind and never joined the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Qian kept his words in mind and never joined the rebels.

sentences.zh: 蕭穎士蕭穎士，字茂挺，梁鄱陽王恢七世孫。

translations.literal: Xiao Yingshi, styled Maoting, was seventh-generation descendant of Prince of Poyang Hui of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yingshi, courtesy name Maoting, was seventh-generation descendant of Prince of Poyang Hui of Liang.

sentences.zh: 祖晶，賢而有謀，任雅相伐高麗，表為記室。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jing was talented and resourceful; serving Ren Yaxiang's campaign against Goguryeo, he was appointed recorder.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jing was talented and resourceful; serving Ren Yaxiang's campaign against Goguryeo, he was appointed recorder.

sentences.zh: 越王貞舉兵，杖策詣之，陳三策，王不用，晶度必敗，乃亡去，客死廣陵。

translations.literal: When Prince of Yue Zhen raised troops, Jing went on foot to join him, presented three strategies — the prince did not use them — Jing judged he would certainly fail and fled; he died as a guest in Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Yue Zhen raised troops, Jing went on foot to join him and presented three strategies — the prince did not use them — Jing judged he would fail and fled; he died as a guest in Guangling.

sentences.zh: 穎士四歲屬文，十歲補太學生。

translations.literal: Yingshi composed prose at four and at ten was enrolled as an Imperial University student.
translations.idiomatic: Yingshi composed prose at four and at ten was enrolled as an imperial university student.

sentences.zh: 觀書一覽即誦，通百家譜系、書籀學。

translations.literal: He read a book once and could recite it; he mastered the genealogies of a hundred families and paleography.
translations.idiomatic: He read a book once and could recite it; he mastered the genealogies of a hundred families and paleography.

sentences.zh: 開元二十三年，舉進士，對策第一。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Kaiyuan he passed the jinshi examination and ranked first in the policy questions.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 23 he passed the jinshi examination and ranked first in the policy questions.

sentences.zh: 父旻，以莒丞抵罪，穎士往訴于府佐張惟一，惟一曰：「旻有佳兒，吾以旻獲譴不憾。

translations.literal: His father Min, as assistant magistrate of Ju, incurred guilt — Yingshi went to plead before the prefectural aide Zhang Weiyi, who said: "Min has an excellent son; I do not regret being punished on Min's account."
translations.idiomatic: His father Min, as assistant magistrate of Ju, incurred guilt — Yingshi went to plead before the prefectural aide Zhang Weiyi, who said, "Min has an excellent son; I do not regret being punished on Min's account."

sentences.zh: 」乃平宥之。

translations.literal: He then fully pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: He then fully pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，穎士補秘書正字。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao Yingshi was appointed Rectifier in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianbao Yingshi was appointed rectifier in the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 于時裴耀卿、席豫、張均、宋遙、韋述皆先進，器其材，與鈞禮，由是名播天下。

translations.literal: At the time Pei Yaoqing, Xi Yu, Zhang Jun, Song Yao, and Wei Shu were all seniors who valued his talent and treated him with ceremony — from then his name spread through the realm.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Pei Yaoqing, Xi Yu, Zhang Jun, Song Yao, and Wei Shu were all seniors who valued his talent and treated him with ceremony — from then his name spread through the realm.

sentences.zh: 奉使括遺書趙、衛間，淹久不報，為有司劾免，留客濮陽。

translations.literal: On a mission to search for lost books in Zhao and Wei he lingered long without reporting back and was impeached and dismissed, staying as a guest in Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: On a mission to search for lost books in Zhao and Wei he lingered long without reporting back and was impeached and dismissed, staying as a guest in Puyang.
